Can anyone fathom the spreading of the clouds,
See how he scatters his lightning over it
By these things he judges the people
He gathers the lightning into his hands
Its crashing announces its presence
“At this, my own heart trembles
Just listen to the rumbling of his voice,
He sends it out under all of heaven,
There follows a sound, a roar —
“God thunders wonderfully with his voice,
He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth!’ —
He brings all human activity to a stop,
Then the animals go into their lairs
“Out of its chamber comes the storm,
By the breath of God, ice is given,
He weighs the clouds down with moisture,
He, by his plans, turns them around,
he brings them forth on the earth
“Listen to this, Iyov!
Do you know how God puts them in place,
Do you know how he balances the clouds?
“You, sweltering in your clothing
can you, with him, spread out the sky,
Teach us what we should tell him,
Is he to be told that I will speak?
Now people don’t see the light,
Out of the north comes a golden glow,
Shaddai, whom we cannot find,
This is why people fear him;
Then Adonai answered Iyov out of the storm:
“Who is this, darkening my plans
Stand up like a man, and brace yourself;
“Where were you when I founded the earth?
Do you know who determined its dimensions
On what were its bases sunk,
when the morning stars sang together,
“Who shut up the sea behind closed doors
when I made the clouds its blanket
when I made the breakers its boundary
and said, ‘You may come this far, but no farther;
“Have you ever in your life called up the dawn
so that it could take hold of the edges of the earth
Then the earth is changed like clay under a seal,
But from the wicked the light is withheld,
“Have you gone down to the springs of the sea
Have the gates of death been revealed to you,
Have you surveyed the full extent of the earth?
“Which way leads to where light has its home?
If you knew, you could take each to its place
You know, of course, because you were born then;
“Have you gone into the storehouses for snow
which I save for times of trouble,
“By what path is light dispersed,
Who cut a channel for the downpours,
causing it to rain where no one is,
drenching the waste and desolate [ground],
Does the rain have a father?
From whose womb does ice come?
when water becomes as hard as stone,
“Can you tie up the cords of the Pleiades
Can you lead out the constellations of the zodiac in their season
Do you know the laws of the sky?
“Can you raise your voice to the clouds
Can you send lightning bolts on their way?
“Who put wisdom in people’s inner parts?
Who, by wisdom, can number the clouds?
so that the dust becomes a mass [of mud],
“Can you hunt prey for a lioness
when they crouch in their dens
Who provides food for the raven
“Do you know when mountain goats give birth?
Can you tell how many months they carry their young?
when they crouch down and bring forth their young,
Their young become strong, growing up in the open;
“Who lets the wild donkey roam freely?
I made the ‘Aravah its home,
It scorns the noise of the city
It ranges over the hills for its pasture,
“Would a wild ox be willing to serve you?
Could you tie a rope around its neck
Would you trust its great strength enough
or rely on it to bring home your seed
“An ostrich’s wings beat wildly,
It leaves its eggs on the ground
forgetting that a foot may crush them
It treats its chicks heartlessly,
because God has deprived it of wisdom
When the time comes, it flaps its wings,
“Did you give the horse its strength?
Did you make him able to leap like a locust?
It paws with force and exults with vigor,
mocking at fear, unafraid,
The [rider’s] quiver rattles over it,
Frenzied and eager, it devours the ground,
At the sound of the shofar it whinnies;
“Is it your wisdom that sets the hawk soaring,
Does the eagle fly up when you say so,
It lives and spends its nights on the cliffs;
From there it spots its prey,
Its young ones suck up blood;
Continuing to address Iyov, Adonai said:
“Does the critic still want to dispute Shaddai?
Then Iyov replied to Adonai:
“I am too ashamed; I have nothing to say.
Yes, I spoke once, but I won’t answer more;
Adonai answered Iyov out of the storm:
“Stand up like a man, and brace yourself;
“Are you impugning my justice?
Do you have an arm like God’s?
Come on, deck yourself with majesty and dignity,
Let loose your furious anger,
Look at all who are proud, and bring them down;
Bury them in the ground together,
If you do this, then I will confess to you
“Now consider Behemot, whom I made along with you.
What strength he has in his loins!
He can make his tail as stiff as a cedar,
his bones are like bronze pipes,
“He ranks first among God’s works.
The mountains produce food for him there,
He lies down under the thorny lotus bushes
the lotus bushes cover him with their shade,
If the river overflows, it doesn’t worry him;
Can anyone catch him by his eyes
“And Livyatan! Can you catch him with a fishhook
Can you put a ring in his nose
Will he entreat you at length?
Will he agree with you
Will you play with him as you would with a bird
Will a group of fishermen turn him into a banquet?
Can you fill his skin with darts
If you lay your hand on him,
“Look, any hope [of capturing him] is futile —
No one is fierce enough to rouse him,
Who has given me anything
“I have more to say about his limbs,
Who can strip off his [scaly] garment?
Who can pry open the doors of his face,
“His pride is his rows of scales,
one is so close to the next
they are stuck one to another,
“When he sneezes, light flashes out;
From his mouth go fiery torches,
His nostrils belch steam
His breath sets coals ablaze;
“Strength resides in his neck,
The layers of his flesh stick together;
His heart is as hard as a stone,
When he rears himself up, the gods are afraid,
“If a sword touches him, it won’t stick;
He regards iron as straw
An arrow can’t make him flee;
Clubs count as hay,
His belly is as sharp as fragments of pottery,
“He makes the depths seethe like a pot,
He leaves a shining wake behind him,
“On earth there is nothing like him,
He looks straight at all high things.
Then [at last,] Iyov gave Adonai this answer:
“I know that you can do everything,
“[You asked,] ‘Who is this, hiding counsel,
“Please listen, and I will speak.
I had heard about you with my ears,
therefore I detest [myself]

After Adonai had spoken these words to Iyov, Adonai said to Elifaz the Teimani, “My anger is blazing against you and your two friends, because, unlike my servant Iyov, you have not spoken rightly about me.

So now, get yourselves seven young bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Iyov, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering. My servant Iyov will pray for you — because him I will accept — so that I won’t punish you as your boorishness deserves; because you have not spoken rightly about me, as my servant Iyov has.”
So Elifaz the Teimani, Bildad the Shuchi and Tzofar the Na‘amati went and did what Adonai had ordered them to do, and Adonai accepted Iyov[’s prayer].
When Iyov prayed for his friends, Adonai restored his fortunes; Adonai gave Iyov twice as much as he had had before.

Then all his brothers and sisters came to him, also all who had known him before, and they ate a meal with him in his house. They consoled and comforted him for all the evils Adonai had inflicted on him. Each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
Adonai blessed Iyov’s later situation even more than his earlier one — he had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
The first he named Y’mimah; the second, K’tzi‘ah; and the third, Keren-Hapukh.
Nowhere in the land could women be found as beautiful as Iyov’s daughters; and their father gave them inheritances along with their brothers.
After this, Iyov lived 140 years, long enough to see his sons and grandsons, four generations.
Then, old and full of days, Iyov died.
How blessed are those
Their delight
They are like trees planted by streams —
Not so the wicked,
For this reason the wicked
For Adonai watches over
Why are the nations in an uproar,
The earth’s kings are taking positions,
They cry, “Let’s break their fetters!
He who sits in heaven laughs;
Then in his anger he rebukes them,
“I myself have installed my king
“I will proclaim the decree:
Ask of me, and I will make
You will break them with an iron rod,
Therefore, kings, be wise;
Serve Adonai with fear;
Kiss the son, lest he be angry,
A psalm of David, when he fled from Avshalom his son:
Adonai, how many enemies I have!
how countless those who say of me,
But you, Adonai, are a shield for me;
With my voice I call out to Adonai,
I lie down and sleep, then wake up again,
I am not afraid of the tens of thousands
Rise up, Adonai!
Victory comes from Adonai;
For the leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David:
O God, my vindicator!
Men of rank, how long will you shame my honor,
Understand that Adonai sets apart
You can be angry, but do not sin!
Offer sacrifices rightly,
Many ask, “Who can show us some good?”
You have filled my heart with more joy
I will lie down and sleep in peace;
For the leader. On wind instruments. A psalm of David:
Give ear to my words, Adonai,
Listen to my cry for help,
Adonai, in the morning you will hear my voice;
For you are not a God
Those who brag cannot stand before your eyes,
you destroy those who tell lies,
But I can enter your house
Lead me, Adonai, in your righteousness
For in their mouths there is nothing sincere,
God, declare them guilty!
But let all who take refuge in you rejoice,
For you, Adonai, bless the righteous;
For the leader. With stringed instruments. On sh’minit [low-pitched musical instruments?]. A psalm of David:
Adonai, don’t rebuke me in your anger,
Be gracious to me, Adonai,
I am completely terrified;
Come back, Adonai, and rescue me!
for in death, no one remembers you;
I am worn out with groaning;
My vision is darkened with anger;
Get away from me, all you workers of evil!
Adonai has heard my pleading,
All my enemies will be confounded,
A shiggayon of David, which he sang to Adonai because of Kush the Ben-Y’mini:
Adonai my God, in you I take refuge.
otherwise, they will maul me like a lion
Adonai my God, if I have caused this,
if I paid back evil to him who was at peace with me,
then let the enemy pursue me
Rise up, Adonai, in your anger!
May the assembly of the peoples surround you;
Adonai, who dispenses judgment to the peoples,
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end,
My shield is God,
God is a righteous judge,
If a person will not repent,
he has also prepared for him
Look how the wicked is pregnant with evil;
He makes a pit, digs it deep,
His mischief will return onto his own head,
I thank Adonai for his righteousness
For the leader. On the gittit. A psalm of David:
Adonai! Our Lord! How glorious
From the mouths of babies and infants at the breast
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers,
what are mere mortals, that you concern yourself with them;
You made him but little lower than the angels,
you had him rule what your hands made,
sheep and oxen, all of them,
the birds in the air, the fish in the sea,
Adonai! Our Lord! How glorious
For the leader. On the death of Labben. A psalm of David:
I give thanks to Adonai with all my heart.
I will be glad and exult in you.
When my enemies turn back,
For you upheld my cause as just,
You rebuked the nations, destroyed the wicked,
The enemy is finished, in ruins forever;
But Adonai is enthroned forever;
He will judge the world in righteousness;
Adonai is a stronghold for the oppressed,
Those who know your name put their trust in you,
Sing praises to Adonai, who lives in Tziyon;
For the avenger of blood remembers them,
“Have mercy on me, Adonai!
so that I can proclaim all your praises
The nations have drowned in the pit they dug,
Adonai made himself known and executed judgment;
The wicked will return to Sh’ol,
For the poor will not always be forgotten
Arise, Adonai! Don’t let mortals prevail!
Strike them with terror, Adonai!
Why, Adonai, do you stand at a distance?
The wicked in their arrogance hunt down the poor,
For the wicked boasts about his lusts;
Every scheme of the wicked in his arrogance [says],
His ways prosper at all times.
In his heart he thinks, “I will never be shaken;
His mouth is full of curses, deceit, oppression;
He waits near settlements in ambush
Lurking unseen like a lion in his lair,
Yes, he stoops, crouches down low;
He says in his heart, “God forgets,
Arise, Adonai! God, raise your hand!
Why does the wicked despise God
You have seen; for you look at mischief and grief,
Break the arm of the wicked!
Adonai is king forever and ever!
Adonai, you have heard what the humble want;
to give justice to the fatherless and oppressed,
For the leader. By David:
See how the wicked are drawing their bows
If the foundations are destroyed,
Adonai is in his holy temple.
Adonai tests the righteous;
He will rain hot coals down on the wicked,
For Adonai is righteous;
For the leader. On sh’minit [low-pitched musical instruments?]. A psalm of David:
Help, Adonai! For no one godly is left;
They all tell lies to each other,
May Adonai cut off all flattering lips
those who say, “By our tongues, we will prevail;
“Because the poor are oppressed,
The words of Adonai are pure words,
You, Adonai, protect us;
the wicked strut about everywhere
For the leader. A psalm of David:
How long, Adonai?
How long must I keep asking myself what to do,
Look, and answer me, Adonai my God!
Then my enemy would say, “I was able to beat him”;
But I trust in your grace,
For the leader. By David:
From heaven Adonai observes humankind
But all turn aside, all alike are corrupt;
Don’t they ever learn,
There they are, utterly terrified;
You may mock the plans of the poor,
How I wish Isra’el’s salvation
A psalm of David:
Those who live a blameless life,
and keep their tongues from slander;
who look with scorn on the vile,
who refuse usury when they lend money
Mikhtam. By David:
I said to Adonai, “You are my Lord;
The holy people in the land are the ones
Those who run after another god
Adonai, my assigned portion, my cup:
Pleasant places were measured out for me;
I bless Adonai, my counselor;
I always set Adonai before me;
so my heart is glad, my glory rejoices,
for you will not abandon me to Sh’ol,
You make me know the path of life;
A prayer of David:
Let my vindication come from you,
You probed my heart,
As for what others do, by words from your lips
my steps hold steadily to your paths,
Now I call on you, God, for you will answer me.
Show how wonderful is your grace,
Protect me like the pupil of your eye,
from the wicked, who are assailing me,
They close their hearts to compassion;
they track me down, they surround me;
They are like lions eager to tear the prey,
Arise, Adonai, confront them! Bring them down!
with your hand, Adonai, from human beings,
But my prayer, in righteousness, is to see your face;

For the leader. By David the servant of Adonai, who addressed the words of this song to Adonai on the day when Adonai delivered him from the power of all his enemies, including from the power of Sha’ul.
He said:
“Adonai is my Rock, my fortress and deliverer,
I call on Adonai, who is worthy of praise;
“For the cords of death surrounded me,
the ropes of Sh’ol were wrapped around me,
In my distress I called to Adonai;
“Then the earth quaked and shook,
Smoke arose in his nostrils;
He lowered heaven and came down
He rode on a keruv; he flew,
He made darkness his hiding-place,
From the brightness before him,
“Adonai also thundered in heaven,
He sent out arrows and scattered them,
The channels of water appeared,
“He sent from on high, he took me
he rescued me from my powerful enemy,
They came against me on my day of disaster,
He brought me out to an open place;
Adonai rewarded me for my uprightness,
“For I have kept the ways of Adonai,
for all his rulings were before me,
I was pure-hearted with him
“Hence Adonai repaid me for my uprightness,
With the merciful, you are merciful;
with the pure, you are pure;
People afflicted, you save;
“For you, Adonai, light my lamp;
With you I can run through a whole troop of men,
“As for God, his way is perfect,
“For who is God but Adonai?
“It is God who girds me with strength;
He makes me swift, sure-footed as a deer,
He trains my hands for war
“You give me your shield, which is salvation,
You lengthen the steps I can take,
“I pursued my enemies and overtook them,
I crushed them, so that they can’t get up;
“For you braced me with strength for the battle
You made my enemies turn their backs in flight,
“They cried out, but there was no one to help,
I pulverized them like dust in the wind,
“You also freed me from the quarrels of my people.
the moment they hear of me, they obey me,
Foreigners lose heart
“Adonai is alive! Blessed is my Rock!
the God who avenges me
He delivers me from my enemies.
“So I give thanks to you, Adonai, among the nations;
Great salvation he gives to his king;
For the leader. A psalm of David:
The heavens declare the glory of God,
Every day it utters speech,
Without speech, without a word,
their line goes out through all the earth
which comes out like a bridegroom from the bridal chamber,
It rises at one side of the sky,
The Torah of Adonai is perfect,
The precepts of Adonai are right,
The fear of Adonai is clean,
more desirable than gold,
Through them your servant is warned;
Who can discern unintentional sins?
Also keep your servant from presumptuous sins,
May the words of my mouth
For the leader. A psalm of David:
May Adonai answer you in times of distress,
May he send you help from the sanctuary
May he be reminded by all your grain offerings
May he grant you your heart’s desire
Then we will shout for joy at your victory
Now I know that Adonai
Some trust in chariots and some in horses,
They will crumple and fall,
Give victory, Adonai!
For the leader. A psalm of David:
Adonai, the king finds joy in your strength;
You give him his heart’s desire;
For you come to meet him with the best blessings,
He asks you for life; you give it to him,
Your victory brings him great glory;
For you bestow on him everlasting blessings,
For the king puts his trust in Adonai,
Your hand will find all your enemies;
At your appearing,
You will destroy from the earth their descendants,
for they intended evil against you;
For you will make them turn their back
Arise, Adonai, in your strength;
For the leader. Set to “Sunrise.” A psalm of David:
My God! My God!
My God, by day I call to you,
Nevertheless, you are holy,
In you our ancestors put their trust;
They cried to you and escaped;
But I am a worm, not a man,
All who see me jeer at me;
“He committed himself to Adonai,
But you are the one who took me from the womb,
Since my birth I’ve been thrown on you;
Don’t stay far from me, for trouble is near;
Many bulls surround me,
They open their mouths wide against me,
I am poured out like water;
my mouth is as dry as a fragment of a pot,
Dogs are all around me,
I can count every one of my bones,
They divide my garments among themselves;
But you, Adonai, don’t stay far away!
Rescue me from the sword,
Save me from the lion’s mouth!
I will proclaim your name to my kinsmen;
“You who fear Adonai, praise him!
For he has not despised or abhorred
Because of you
The poor will eat and be satisfied;
All the ends of the earth
For the kingdom belongs to Adonai,
All who prosper on the earth
A descendant will serve him;
They will come and proclaim
A psalm of David:
He has me lie down in grassy pastures,
he restores my inner person.
Even if I pass through death-dark ravines,
You prepare a table for me,
Goodness and grace will pursue me
By David. A psalm:
for he set its foundations on the seas
Who may go up to the mountain of Adonai?
Those with clean hands and pure hearts,
They will receive a blessing from Adonai
Such is the character of those who seek him,
Lift up your heads, you gates!
Who is he, this glorious king?
Lift up your heads, you gates!
Who is he, this glorious king?
By David:
I trust you, my God.
No one waiting for you will be disgraced;
Make me know your ways, Adonai,
Guide me in your truth, and teach me;
Remember your compassion and grace, Adonai;
Don’t remember my youthful sins or transgressions;
Adonai is good, and he is fair;
leads the humble to do what is right
All Adonai’s paths are grace and truth
For the sake of your name, Adonai,
Who is the person who fears Adonai?
He will remain prosperous,
Adonai relates intimately with those who fear him;
My eyes are always directed toward Adonai,
Turn to me, and show me your favor;
The troubles of my heart are growing and growing;
See my affliction and suffering,
Consider my enemies, how many there are
Protect me and rescue me;
Let integrity and uprightness preserve me,
God! Redeem Isra’el
By David:
Examine me, Adonai, test me,
For your grace is there before my eyes,
I have not sat with worthless folks,
I hate the company of evildoers,
I will wash my hands in innocence
lifting my voice in thanks
Adonai, I love the house where you live,
Don’t include me with sinners
In their hands are evil schemes;
As for me, I will live a blameless life.
My feet are planted on level ground;
By David:
When evildoers assailed me
If an army encamps against me,
Just one thing have I asked of Adonai;
For he will conceal me in his shelter
Then my head will be lifted up
Listen, Adonai, to my voice when I cry;
“My heart said of you, ‘Seek my face.’”
Do not hide your face from me,
Even though my father and mother have left me,
Teach me your way, Adonai;
don’t give me up to the whims of my foes;
If I hadn’t believed that I would see
Put your hope in Adonai, be strong,
By David:
Hear the sound of my prayers
Don’t drag me off with the wicked,
Pay them back for their deeds,
For they don’t understand the deeds of Adonai
Blessed be Adonai,
Adonai is my strength and shield;
Adonai is strength for [his people],
Save your people! Bless your heritage!
A psalm of David:
give Adonai the glory due his name;
The voice of Adonai is over the waters;
the voice of Adonai in power,
The voice of Adonai cracks the cedars;
and makes the L’vanon skip like a calf,
The voice of Adonai flashes fiery flames;
the voice of Adonai rocks the desert,
The voice of Adonai causes deer to give birth
Adonai sits enthroned above the flood!
May Adonai give strength to his people!
A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. By David:
I will exalt you, Adonai, because you drew me up;
Adonai my God, I cried out to you,
Adonai, you lifted me up from Sh’ol;
Sing praise to Adonai, you faithful of his;
For his anger is momentary,
Once I was prosperous and used to say,
when you showed me favor, Adonai,
I called to you, Adonai;
“What advantage is there in my death,
Hear me, Adonai, and show me your favor!
You turned my mourning into dancing!
so that my well-being can praise you and not be silent;
For the leader. A psalm of David:
In you, Adonai, I take refuge;
Turn your ear toward me,
Since you are my rock and fortress,
Free me from the net they have hidden to catch me,
Into your hand I commit my spirit;
I hate those who serve worthless idols;
I will rejoice and be glad in your grace,
You did not hand me over to the enemy;
Show me favor, Adonai, for I am in trouble.
For my life is worn out with sorrow
I am scorned by all my adversaries,
Like a dead man, I have passed from their minds;
All I hear is whispering,
But I, I trust in you, Adonai;
My times are in your hand;
Make your face shine on your servant;
Adonai, don’t let me be put to shame,
May lying lips be struck dumb,
But oh, how great is your goodness,
In the shelter of your presence
Blessed be Adonai!
As for me, in my alarm I said,
Love Adonai, you faithful of his.
Be strong, and fill your hearts with courage,
By David. A maskil:
How blessed those to whom Adonai imputes no guilt,
When I kept silent, my bones wasted away
day and night your hand was heavy on me;
When I acknowledged my sin to you,
This is what everyone faithful should pray
You are a hiding-place for me,
“I will instruct and teach you
Don’t be like a horse or mule
Many are the torments of the wicked,
Be glad in Adonai; rejoice, you righteous!
Rejoice in Adonai, you righteous!
Give thanks to Adonai with the lyre,
Sing to him a new song,
For the word of Adonai is true,
He loves righteousness and justice;
By the word of Adonai the heavens were made,
He collects the sea waters together in a heap;
Let all the earth fear Adonai!
For he spoke, and there it was;
Adonai brings to nothing the plans of nations,
But the counsel of Adonai stands forever,
How blessed is the nation whose God is Adonai,
Adonai looks out from heaven;
from the place where he lives
he who fashioned the hearts of them all
A king is not saved by the size of his army,
To rely on a horse for safety is vain,
But Adonai’s eyes watch over those who fear him,
to rescue them from death
We are waiting for Adonai;
For in him our hearts rejoice,
May your mercy, Adonai, be over us,
By David, when he pretended to be insane before Avimelekh, who then drove him away; so he left:
I will bless Adonai at all times;
When I boast, it will be about Adonai;
Proclaim with me the greatness of Adonai;
I sought Adonai, and he answered me;
They looked to him and grew radiant;
This poor man cried; Adonai heard
The angel of Adonai, who encamps
Taste, and see that Adonai is good.
Fear Adonai, you holy ones of his,
Young lions can be needy, they can go hungry,
Come, children, listen to me;
Which of you takes pleasure in living?
[If you do,] keep your tongue from evil
turn from evil, and do good;
The eyes of Adonai watch over the righteous,
But the face of Adonai opposes those who do evil,
[The righteous] cried out, and Adonai heard,
Adonai is near those with broken hearts;
The righteous person suffers many evils,
He protects all his bones;
Evil will kill the wicked,
But Adonai redeems his servants;
By David:
Grasp your shield and protective gear,
Brandish spear and battle-axe
May those who seek my life
May they be like chaff before the wind,
May their way be dark and slippery,
For unprovoked, they hid their net over a pit;
May destruction come over him unawares.
Then I will be joyful in Adonai,
All my bones will say,
Malicious witnesses come forward,
They repay me evil for good;
But I, when they were ill, wore sackcloth;
I behaved as I would for my friend or my brother;
But when I stumble, they gather in glee;
With ungodly mocking and grimacing,
Adonai, how much longer will you look on?
I will give you thanks in the great assembly,
Don’t let those who are wrongfully my enemies
For they don’t speak words of peace
They shout to accuse me, “Aha! Aha!
You saw them, Adonai; don’t stay silent.
Wake up! Get up, my God, my Lord!
Give judgment for me, Adonai, my God,
Don’t let them say to themselves,
May those who gloat over my distress
But may those who delight in my righteousness
Then my tongue will tell of your righteousness
For the leader. By David, the servant of Adonai:
Crime speaks to the wicked.
For, the way he sees it,
His words are wrong and deceitful;
He devises trouble as he lies in bed;
Adonai, in the heavens is your grace;
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God,
How precious, God, is your grace!
they feast on the rich bounty of your house,
For with you is the fountain of life;
Continue your grace to those who know you
Don’t let the foot of the proud tread on me
There they lie fallen, those evildoers,
By David:
for soon they will wither like grass
Trust in Adonai, and do good;
Then you will delight yourself in Adonai,
Commit your way to Adonai;
He will make your vindication shine forth like light,
Be still before Adonai;
Stop being angry, put aside rage,
For evildoers will be cut off,
Soon the wicked will be no more;
But the meek will inherit the land
The wicked plots against the righteous
but Adonai laughs at the wicked,
The wicked have unsheathed their swords,
But their swords will pierce their own hearts,
Better the little that the righteous has
For the arms of the wicked will be broken,
Adonai knows what the wholehearted suffer,
They will not be distressed when times are hard;
For the wicked will perish;
The wicked borrows and doesn’t repay,
For those blessed by [Adonai] will inherit the land,
Adonai directs a person’s steps,
He may stumble, but he won’t fall headlong,
I have been young; now I am old;
All day long he is generous and lends,
If you turn from evil and do good,
For Adonai loves justice
The righteous will inherit the land
The mouth of the righteous articulates wisdom,
The Torah of his God is in his heart;
The wicked keeps his eye on the righteous,
But Adonai will not leave him in his power
Put your hope in Adonai, keep to his way,
I have seen a wicked man wielding great power,
But I passed by again, and he was no longer there;
Observe the pure person, consider the upright;
But transgressors will all be destroyed;
Adonai is the one who saves the righteous;
Adonai helps them and rescues them,
A psalm of David, serving as a reminder:
Adonai, don’t rebuke me when you are angry
for your arrows penetrate me deeply,
Your indignation left no part of me intact;
for my iniquities loom high over my head
I have stinking, festering wounds
I am bent down, prostrate completely;
For my insides burn with fever,
I am numb, completely crushed;
Adonai, all my longing is known to you;
My heart is throbbing, my strength is gone,
My friends and companions shun my disease;
Those seeking my life lay snares for me,
But I’m like a deaf man — I don’t hear it;
Yes, I’ve become like a man who doesn’t hear
For it is in you, Adonai, that I hope.
I said, “Don’t let them gloat over me
For I am about to fall,
I acknowledge my guilt,
But my enemies are alive and well,
and, since they repay good with evil,
Don’t abandon me, Adonai!
Come quickly to help me,
For the leader. Set in the style of Y’dutun. A psalm of David:
I said, “I will watch how I behave,
I was silent, said nothing, not even good;
My heart grew hot within me;
“Make me grasp, Adonai, what my end must be,
You have made my days like handbreadths;
Humans go about like shadows;
Now, Adonai, what am I waiting for?
Rescue me from all my transgressions;
I am silent, I keep my mouth shut,
Stop raining blows on me;
With rebukes you discipline people for their guilt;
Hear my prayer, Adonai, listen to my cry,
Turn your gaze from me, so I can smile again
For the leader. A psalm of David:
I waited patiently for Adonai,
He brought me up from the roaring pit,
He put a new song in my mouth,
How blessed the man who trusts in Adonai
How much you have done, Adonai my God!
Sacrifices and grain offerings you don’t want;
so then I said, “Here I am! I’m coming!
Doing your will, my God, is my joy;
I have proclaimed what is right in the great assembly;
I did not hide your righteousness in my heart
Adonai, don’t withhold your mercy from me.
For numberless evils surround me;
Be pleased, Adonai, to rescue me!
May those who seek to sweep me away
May those who jeer at me, “Aha! Aha!”
But may all those who seek you
But I am poor and needy;
For the leader. A psalm of David:
How blessed are those who care for the poor!
Adonai will preserve them, keep them alive,
Adonai sustains them on their sickbed;
I said, “Adonai, have pity on me!
My enemies say the worst about me:
When they come to see me they speak insincerely,
All who hate me whisper together against me,
“A fatal disease has attached itself to him;
Even my close friend, on whom I relied,
But you, Adonai, have pity on me,
I will know you are pleased with me
You uphold me because of my innocence
Blessed be Adonai the God of Isra’el
For the leader. A maskil of the descendants of Korach:
Just as a deer longs for running streams,
I am thirsty for God, for the living God!
My tears are my food, day and night,
I recall, as my feelings well up within me,
My soul, why are you so downcast?
My God, when I feel so downcast,
Deep is calling to deep
By day Adonai commands his grace,
I say to God my Rock,
My adversaries’ taunts make me feel
My soul, why are you so downcast?
Judge me, God, and plead my cause
For you are the God of my strength;
Send out your light and your truth;
Then I will go to the altar of God,
My soul, why are you so downcast?
For the leader. By the descendants of Korach. A maskil:
God, we heard it with our ears;
With your hand you drove out nations
For not by their own swords
God, you are my king;
Through you we pushed away our foes,
For I don’t rely on my bow,
No, you saved us from our adversaries;
We will boast in our God all day
Yet now you have thrust us aside and disgraced us;
You make us retreat from the adversary,
You have handed us over like sheep to be eaten
You sell your people for a pittance,
You make us an object for our neighbors to mock,
You make us a byword among the nations;
All day long my disgrace is on my mind,
at the sound of those who revile and insult,
Though all this came on us, we did not forget you;
Our hearts have not turned back,
though you pressed us into a lair of jackals
If we had forgotten the name of our God
wouldn’t God have discovered this,
For your sake we are put to death all day long,
Wake up, Adonai! Why are you asleep?
Why are you turning your face away,
For we are lying flat in the dust,
Get up, and come to help us!
For the leader. Set to “Lilies.” By the descendants of Korach. A maskil. A lovesong:
My heart is stirred by a noble theme;
You are the most handsome of men;
Warrior, strap your sword at your thigh;
In your majesty, succeed, ride on
Your arrows are sharp. The people fall under you,
Your throne, God, will last forever and ever;
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness.
Your robes are all fragrant with myrrh, aloes and cassia;
Daughters of kings are among your favorites;
Listen, daughter! Think, pay attention!
and the king will desire your beauty;
Then the daughter of Tzor, the richest of peoples,
Inside [the palace], the king’s daughter looks splendid,
In brocade, she will be led to the king,
They will be led in with gladness and joy,
You will have sons to succeed your ancestors;
I will make your name known through all generations;
For the leader. By the descendants of Korach. On ‘alamot [high-pitched musical instruments?]. A song:
God is our refuge and strength,
Therefore we are unafraid,
even if its waters rage and foam,
There is a river whose streams
God is in the city.
Nations were in turmoil,
Adonai-Tzva’ot is with us,
Come and see the works of Adonai,
To the ends of the earth he makes wars cease —
“Desist, and learn that I am God,
Adonai-Tzva’ot is with us,
For the leader. A psalm of the descendants of Korach:
Clap your hands, all you peoples!
For Adonai ‘Elyon is awesome,
He makes peoples subject to us,
He chooses our heritage for us,
God goes up to shouts of acclaim,
Sing praises to God, sing praises!
For God is king of all the earth;
God rules the nations;
The leaders of the people gather together,
A song. A psalm of the descendants of Korach:
Great is Adonai
beautiful in its elevation,
In its citadels God
For the kings met by agreement;
They saw and were filled with consternation;
Trembling took hold of them,
as when the wind out of the east
We heard it, and now we see for ourselves
God, within your temple
God, your praise, like your name,
Let Mount Tziyon rejoice,
Walk through Tziyon, go all around it;
Note its ramparts, pass through its citadels,
that such is God, our God forever;
For the leader. A psalm of the descendants of Korach:
Hear this, all you peoples!
regardless of whether low or high,
My mouth is about to speak wisdom;
I will listen with care to [God’s] parable,
Why should I fear when the days bring trouble,
the evil of those who rely on their wealth
No one can ever redeem his brother
because the price for him is too high
to have him live on eternally
For he can see that wise men will die,
They think their homes will last forever,
But people, even rich ones, will live only briefly;
This is the manner of life of the foolish
Like sheep, they are destined for Sh’ol;
But God will redeem me from Sh’ol’s control,
Don’t be afraid when someone gets rich,
For when he dies, he won’t take it with him;
True, while he lived, he thought himself happy —
but he will join his ancestors’ generations
People, even rich ones, can fail to grasp
A psalm of Asaf:
Out of Tziyon, the perfection of beauty,
Our God is coming and not staying silent.
he calls to the heavens above and to earth,
“Gather to me my faithful,
The heavens proclaim his righteousness,
“Listen, my people, I am speaking:
I am not rebuking you for your sacrifices;
I have no need for a bull from your farm
for all forest creatures are mine already,
I know all the birds in the mountains;
If I were hungry, I would not tell you;
Do I eat the flesh of bulls
Offer thanksgiving as your sacrifice to God,
and call on me when you are in trouble;
But to the wicked God says:
when you so hate to receive instruction
When you see a thief, you join up with him,
you give your mouth free rein for evil
you sit and speak against your kinsman,
When you do such things, should I stay silent?
Consider this, you who forget God,
“Whoever offers thanksgiving
For the leader. A psalm of David,
when Natan the prophet came to him after his affair with Bat-Sheva:
God, in your grace, have mercy on me;
Wash me completely from my guilt,
For I know my crimes,
Against you, you only, have I sinned
True, I was born guilty,
Still, you want truth in the inner person;
Sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be clean;
Let me hear the sound of joy and gladness,
Turn away your face from my sins,
Create in me a clean heart, God;
Don’t thrust me away from your presence,
Restore my joy in your salvation,
Then I will teach the wicked your ways,
Rescue me from the guilt of shedding blood,
Adonai, open my lips;
For you don’t want sacrifices, or I would give them;
My sacrifice to God is a broken spirit;
In your good pleasure, make Tziyon prosper;
Then you will delight in righteous sacrifices,
For the leader. A maskil of David,
when Do’eg from Edom came and told Sha’ul, “David has arrived at the house of Achimelekh”:
Why do you boast of your evil, you tyrant,
Your tongue, as sharp as a razor,
You love evil more than good,
You love all words that eat people up,
This is why God will strike you down,
The righteous will see and be awestruck;
“This fellow would not make God his refuge,
But I am like a leafy olive tree
I will praise you forever for what you have done,
For the leader. On machalat. A maskil of David:
A brutish fool tells himself,
God looks out from heaven
Every one of them is unclean,
Won’t these evildoers ever learn?
They will be gripped with terror,
If only salvation for Isra’el
For the leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David,
when the Zifim came and told Sha’ul, “David is hiding with us”:
God, deliver me by your name;
God, hear my prayer;
For foreigners are rising against me,
But God is helping me;
May he repay the evil
Then I will generously sacrifice to you;
because he rescued me from all trouble,
For the leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David:
Listen, God, to my prayer!
Pay attention to me, and answer me!
at how the enemy shouts,
My heart within me is pounding in anguish,
fear and trembling overwhelm me,
I said, “I wish I had wings like a dove!
Yes, I would flee to a place far off,
I would quickly find me a shelter
Confuse, Adonai, confound their speech!
Day and night they go about its walls;
Ruin is rife within it,
For it was not an enemy who insulted me;
But it was you, a man of my own kind,
We used to share our hearts with each other;
May he put death on them;
But I will call on God,
Evening, morning and noon I complain
He redeems me and gives me peace,
God will hear and will humble them,
[My companion] attacked those
What he said sounded smoother than butter,
Unload your burden on Adonai,
But you will bring them down, God,
For the leader. Set to “The Silent Dove in the Distance.” By David; a mikhtam, when the P’lishtim captured him in Gat:
Show me favor, God;
Those who are lying in wait for me
when I am afraid,
In God — I praise his word —
All day long they twist my words;
They gather together and hide themselves,
Because of their crime, they cannot escape;
You have kept count of my wanderings;
Then my enemies will turn back
In God — I praise his word —
in God I trust; I have no fear;
God, I have made vows to you;
For you rescued me from death,
For the leader. Set to “Do Not Destroy.” By David, a mikhtam, when he fled from Sha’ul into the cave:
Show me favor, God, show me favor;
I call to God, the Most High,
He will send from heaven and save me
I am surrounded by lions,
Be exalted, God, above heaven!
They prepared a snare for my feet,
My heart is steadfast, God, steadfast.
Awake, my glory! Awake, lyre and lute!
I will thank you, Adonai, among the peoples;
For your grace is great, all the way to heaven,
Be exalted, God, above heaven!
For the leader. Set to “Do Not Destroy.” By David, a mikhtam:
[Rulers,] does your silence really speak justice?
[No!] In your hearts you devise wrongs,
From the womb, the wicked are estranged,
Their venom is like snake’s venom;
so as not to hear the voice of the charmer,
God, break their teeth in their mouth!
May they vanish like water that drains away.
May they be like a slug that melts as it moves,
Before your cook-pots feel the heat of the burning thorns,
The righteous will rejoice to see vengeance done,
and people will say, “Yes, the righteous are rewarded;
For the leader. Set to “Do Not Destroy.” By David; a mikhtam, when Sha’ul sent men to keep watch on David’s house in order to kill him:
My God, rescue me from my enemies!
Rescue me from evildoers,
For there they are, lying in wait to kill me.
For no fault of mine, they run and prepare.
You, Adonai Elohei-Tzva’ot,
They return at nightfall, snarling like dogs
Look what pours out of their mouth,
But you, Adonai, laugh at them,
My Strength, I will watch for you,
God, who gives me grace, will come to me;
Don’t kill them, or my people will forget;
for the sins their mouths make with each word from their lips.
Finish them off in wrath,
They return at nightfall, snarling like dogs
They roam about, looking for food,
But as for me, I will sing of your strength;
My Strength, I will sing praises to you,
For the leader. Set to “Lily of Testimony.” A mikhtam of David for teaching about
when he fought with Aram-Naharayim and with Aram-Tzovah, and Yo’av returned and killed 12,000 from Edom in the Salt Valley:
God, you rejected us; you crushed us;
You made the land shake, split it apart;
You made your people suffer hard times,
To those who fear you because of the truth
so that those you love could be rescued;
God in his holiness spoke,
Gil‘ad is mine and M’nasheh mine,
Mo’av is my washpot; on Edom I throw my shoe;
Who will bring me into the fortified city?
God, have you rejected us?
Help us against our enemy,
With God’s help we will fight valiantly,
For the leader. With stringed instruments. By David:
Hear my cry, God;
From the end of the earth, with fainting heart,
For you have been a refuge for me,
I will live in your tent forever
For you, God, have heard my vows;
Prolong the life of the king!
May he be enthroned in God’s presence forever!
Then I will sing praise to your name forever,
For the leader. Set in the style of Y’dutun. A psalm of David:
My soul waits in silence for God alone;
He alone is my rock and salvation,
How long will you assail a person
They only want to shake him from his height,
My soul, wait in silence for God alone,
He alone is my rock and salvation,
My safety and honor rest on God.
Trust in him, people, at all times;
Ordinary folks are merely a breath
Don’t put your trust in extortion,
God has spoken once, I have heard it twice:
Also to you, Adonai, belongs grace;
A psalm of David, when he was in the desert of Y’hudah:
O God, you are my God;
I used to contemplate you in the sanctuary,
for your grace is better than life.
Yes, I will bless you as long as I live;
I am as satisfied as with rich food;
when I remember you on my bed
For you have been my help;
my heart clings to you;
But those who seek to destroy my life —
May they be given over to the power of the sword;
But the king will rejoice in God.
For the leader. A psalm of David:
Hear my voice, God, as I plead:
Hide me from the secret intrigues of the wicked
They sharpen their tongues like a sword;
in order to shoot from cover at the innocent,
They support each other’s evil plans;
They search for ways to commit crimes,
Suddenly God shoots them down with an arrow,
their own tongues make them stumble.
Everyone is awestruck —
The righteous will rejoice in Adonai;
For the leader. A psalm of David. A song:
To you, God, in Tziyon, silence is praise;
You who listen to prayer,
When deeds of wickedness overwhelm me,
How blessed are those you choose and bring near,
It is just that you answer us with awesome deeds,
By your strength you set up the mountains.
You still the roaring of the seas,
This is why those living at the ends of the earth
You care for the earth and water it,
Soaking its furrows and settling its soil,
You crown the year with your goodness,
The desert pastures drip water,
the meadows are clothed with flocks
For the leader. A song. A psalm:
Sing the glory of his name,
Tell God, “How awesome are your deeds!
All the earth bows down to you,
Come and see what God has done,
He turned the sea into dry land.
With his power he rules forever;
Bless our God, you peoples!
He preserves our lives
For you, God, have tested us,
You brought us into the net
You made men ride over our heads;
I will come into your house with burnt offerings,
those my lips pronounced and my mouth spoke
I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals,
Come and listen, all you who fear God,
I cried out to him with my mouth,
Had I cherished evil thoughts,
But in fact, God did listen;
Blessed be God, who did not reject my prayer
For the leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song:
God, be gracious to us, and bless us.
so that your way may be known on earth,
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God;
Let the nations be glad and shout for joy,
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God;
The earth has yielded its harvest;
May God continue to bless us,
For the leader. A psalm of David. A song:
Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered;
Drive them away as smoke is driven away;
But let the righteous rejoice and be glad in God’s presence;
Sing to God, sing praises to his name;
God in his holy dwelling,
God gives homes to those who are alone
God, when you went out at the head of your people,
the earth quaked, and rain poured from the sky,
You rained down showers in plenty, God;
Your flock settled in it;
Adonai gives the command;
Kings and their armies are fleeing, fleeing,
Even if you lie among the animal stalls,
When Shaddai scatters kings there,
You mighty mountain, Mount Bashan!
You rugged mountain, why look with envy
God’s chariots are myriads, repeated thousands;
After you went up into the heights,
Blessed be Adonai!
Our God is a God who saves;
God will surely crush the heads of his enemies,
Adonai said, “I will bring them back from Bashan,
so that you can wash your feet in their blood,
They see your processions, God,
The singers are in front, the musicians last,
“In choruses, bless God, Adonai,
There is Binyamin, the youngest, at the head;
God, summon your strength!
from your temple in Yerushalayim,
Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds,
Let envoys come from Egypt,
Sing to God, kingdoms of the earth!
to him who rides on the most ancient heavens.
Acknowledge that strength belongs to God,
How awe-inspiring you are, God,
For the leader. Set to “Lilies.” By David:
Save me, God!
I am sinking down in the mud,
I am exhausted from crying,
Those who hate me for no reason
God, you know how foolish I am;
Let those who put their hope in you,
For your sake I suffer insults,
I am estranged from my brothers,
because zeal for your house is eating me up,
I weep bitterly, and I fast,
I clothe myself with sackcloth
the gossip of those sitting by the town gate,
As for me, Adonai, let my prayer to you
Rescue me from the mud!
Don’t let the floodwaters overwhelm me,
Answer me, Adonai, for your grace is good;
Don’t hide your face from your servant,
Come near to me, and redeem me;
You know how I am insulted,
Insults have broken my heart
They put poison in my food;
Let their dining table
let their eyes be darkened,
Pour out your fury on them,
Let the place where they live be desolate,
for persecuting someone you had already stricken,
Add guilt to their guilt,
Erase them from the book of life,
Meanwhile, I am afflicted and hurting;
I will praise God’s name with a song
This will please Adonai more than a bull,
The afflicted will see it and rejoice;
For Adonai pays attention to the needy
Let heaven and earth praise him,
For God will save Tziyon,
The descendants of his servants will inherit it,
For the leader. By David. As a reminder:
God, rescue me!
May those who seek my life
May those who jeer, “Aha! Aha!”
But may all those who seek you
But I am poor and needy;
In you, Adonai, I have taken refuge;
In your righteousness, rescue me;
Be for me a sheltering rock,
My God, help me escape from the power of the wicked,
For you are my hope, Adonai Elohim,
From birth I have relied on you;
To many, I am an amazing example;
My mouth is full of praise for you,
Don’t reject me when I grow old;
For my enemies are talking about me,
They say, “God has abandoned him;
God, don’t distance yourself from me!
May those who are opposed to me
But I, I will always hope
All day long my mouth will tell
I will come in the power of Adonai Elohim
God, you have taught me since I was young,
So now that I’m old, and my hair is gray,
your righteousness too, God,
You have made me see much trouble and hardship,
You will increase my honor;
As for me, I will praise you with a lyre
My lips will shout for joy;
All day long my tongue
By Shlomo:
so that he can govern your people rightly
May mountains and hills provide your people
May he defend the oppressed among the people,
May they fear you as long as the sun endures
May he be like rain falling on mown grass,
In his days, let the righteous flourish
May his empire stretch from sea to sea,
May desert-dwellers bow before him;
The kings of Tarshish and the coasts will pay him tribute;
Yes, all kings will prostrate themselves before him;
For he will rescue the needy when they cry,
He will have pity on the poor and needy;
He will redeem them from oppression and violence;
May [the king] live long!
May there be an abundance of grain in the land,
May his name endure forever,
Blessed be Adonai, God,
Blessed be his glorious name forever,
This completes the prayers of David the son of Yishai.
A psalm of Asaf:
But as for me, I lost my balance,
when I grew envious of the arrogant
For when their death comes, it is painless;
they don’t have ordinary people’s troubles,
So for them, pride is a necklace;
Their eyes peep out through folds of fat;
They scoff and speak with malice,
They set their mouths against heaven;
Therefore his people return here
Then they ask, “How does God know?
Yes, this is what the wicked are like;
It’s all for nothing that I’ve kept my heart clean
for all day long I am plagued;
If I had said, “I will talk like them,”
When I tried to understand all this,
until I went into the sanctuaries of God
Indeed, you place them on a slippery slope
How suddenly they are destroyed,
They are like a dream when one awakens;
When I had a sour attitude
I was too stupid to understand;
Nevertheless, I am always with you;
You will guide me with your advice;
Whom do I have in heaven but you?
My mind and body may fail; but God
Those who are far from you will perish;
But for me, the nearness of God is my good;
A maskil of Asaf:
Remember your community, which you acquired long ago,
Hurry your steps to these endless ruins,
The roar of your foes filled your meeting-place;
The place seemed like a thicket of trees
With hatchet and hammer they banged away,
They set your sanctuary on fire,
They said to themselves, “We will oppress them completely.”
We see no signs, there is no prophet any more;
How much longer, God, will the foe jeer at us?
Why do you hold back your hand?
God has been my king from earliest times,
By your strength you split the sea in two,
you crushed the heads of Livyatan
You cut channels for springs and streams,
The day is yours, and the night is yours;
It was you who fixed all the limits of the earth,
Remember how the enemy scoffs at Adonai,
Don’t hand over the soul of your dove to wild beasts,
Look to the covenant, for the land’s dark places
Don’t let the oppressed retreat in confusion;
Arise, God, and defend your cause;
Don’t forget what your foes are saying,
For the leader. Set to “Do Not Destroy!” A psalm of Asaf. A song:
We give thanks to you, God, we give thanks;
“At the time of my own choice,
When the earth quakes, with all living on it,
To the boastful I say, “Do not boast!”
Don’t flaunt your strength so proudly;
For you will not be raised to power
since God is the judge; and it is he
In Adonai’s hand there is a cup of wine,
But I will always speak out,
I will break down the strength of the wicked,
For the leader. With string music. A psalm of Asaf. A song:
In Y’hudah God is known;
His tent is in Shalem,
There he broke the flashing arrows,
You are glorious, majestic,
The bravest have been stripped of their spoil
At your rebuke, God of Ya‘akov,
You are fearsome! When once you are angry,
You pronounce sentence from heaven;
when God arises to judge,
Human wrath serves only to praise you;
Make vows to Adonai your God, and keep them;
He curbs the spirit of princes;
For the leader. For Y’dutun. A psalm of Asaf:
I cry aloud to God,
On the day of my distress I am seeking Adonai;
When remembering God, I moan;
You hold my eyelids [and keep me from sleeping];
I think about the days of old,
in the night I remember my song,
“Will Adonai reject forever?
Has his grace permanently disappeared?
Has God forgotten to be compassionate?
Then I add, “That’s my weakness —
So I will remind myself of Yah’s doings;
I will meditate on your work
God, your way is in holiness.
You are the God who does wonders,
With your arm you redeemed your people,
The water saw you, God;
The clouds poured water, the skies thundered,
The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind,
Your way went through the sea,
You led your people like a flock
A maskil of Asaf:
I will speak to you in parables
The things which we have heard and known,
we will not hide from their descendants;
He raised up a testimony in Ya‘akov
so that the next generation would know it,
who could then put their confidence in God,
Then they would not be like their ancestors,
The people of Efrayim, though armed with bows and arrows,
They did not keep the covenant of God
They forgot what he had done,
He had done wonderful things
He split the sea and made them pass through,
He also led them by day with a cloud
He broke apart the rocks in the desert
yes, he brought streams out of the rock,
Yet they sinned still more against him,
in their hearts they tested God
Yes, they spoke against God by asking,
True, he struck the rock, and water gushed out,
Therefore, when Adonai heard, he was angry;
because they had no faith in God,
So he commanded the skies above
He rained down man on them as food;
mortals ate the bread of angels;
He stirred up the east wind in heaven,
and rained down meat on them like dust,
He let them fall in the middle of their camp,
So they ate till they were satisfied;
They were still fulfilling their craving,
when the anger of God rose up against them
Still, they kept on sinning
Therefore, he ended their days in futility
When he brought death among them, they would seek him;
remembering that God was their Rock,
But they tried to deceive him with their words,
for their hearts were not right with him,
Yet he, because he is full of compassion,
So he remembered that they were but flesh,
How often they rebelled against him in the desert
Repeatedly they challenged God
They didn’t remember how he used his hand
how he displayed his signs in Egypt,
He turned their rivers into blood,
He sent swarms of flies, which devoured them,
He gave their harvest to shearer-worms,
He destroyed their vineyards with hail
Their cattle too he gave over to the hail
He sent over them his fierce anger,
to clear a path for his wrath.
striking all the firstborn in Egypt,
But his own people he led out like sheep,
He led them safely, and they weren’t afraid,
He brought them to his holy land,
He expelled nations before them,
Yet they tested El ‘Elyon
They turned away and were faithless, like their fathers;
They provoked him with their high places
God heard, and he was angry;
He abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh,
He gave his strength into exile,
He gave his people over to the sword
Fire consumed their young men,
their cohanim fell by the sword,
Then Adonai awoke, as if from sleep,
He struck his foes, driving them back
Rejecting the tents of Yosef
he chose the tribe of Y’hudah,
He built his sanctuary like the heights;
He chose David to be his servant,
from tending nursing ewes he brought him
With upright heart he shepherded them
A psalm of Asaf:
They have given the corpses of your servants
All around Yerushalayim
We suffer the taunts of our neighbors,
How long, Adonai?
Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t know you,
for they have devoured Ya‘akov
Don’t count past iniquities against us,
Help us, God of our salvation,
Why should the nations ask,
Let the groaning of the captives come before you;
Repay our neighbors sevenfold where they can feel it
Then we, your people and the flock in your pasture,
For the leader. Set to “Lilies.” A testimony. A psalm of Asaf:
Shepherd of Isra’el, listen!
Before Efrayim, Binyamin and M’nasheh,
God, restore us!
Adonai, God of armies, how long
You have fed them tears as their bread
You make our neighbors fight over us,
God of armies, restore us!
You brought a vine out of Egypt,
you cleared a space for it;
The mountains were covered with its shade,
It put out branches as far as the sea
Why did you break down [the vineyard’s] wall,
The boar from the forest tears it apart;
God of armies, please come back!
Protect what your right hand planted,
It is burned by fire, it is cut down;
Help the man at your right hand,
Then we won’t turn away from you —
Adonai, God of armies, restore us!
For the Leader. On the gittit. By Asaf:
Sing for joy to God our strength!
Start the music! Beat the drum!
Sound the shofar at Rosh-Hodesh
because this is a law for Isra’el,
He placed it as a testimony in Y’hosef
“I lifted the load from his shoulder;
You called out when you were in trouble,
“‘Hear, my people, while I give you warning!
There is not to be with you any foreign god;
I am Adonai your God,
“But my people did not listen to my voice;
So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts,
How I wish my people would listen to me,
I would quickly subdue their enemies
Those who hate Adonai would cringe before him,
They would be fed with the finest wheat,
A psalm of Asaf:
“How long will you go on judging unfairly,
Give justice to the weak and fatherless!
Rescue the destitute and needy;
They don’t know, they don’t understand,
“My decree is: ‘You are elohim [gods, judges],
Nevertheless, you will die like mortals;
Rise up, Elohim, and judge the earth;
A song. A psalm of Asaf:
God, don’t remain silent!
because here are your enemies, causing an uproar;
craftily conspiring against your people,
They say, “Come, let’s wipe them out as a nation;
With one mind they plot their schemes;
the tents of Edom and the Yishma‘elim,
G’val, ‘Amon and ‘Amalek,
Ashur too is allied with them,
Do to them as you did to Midyan,
they were destroyed at ‘Ein-Dor
Make their leaders like ‘Orev and Ze’ev,
who said, “Let’s take possession
My God, make them like whirling dust,
Like fire burning up the forest,
drive them away with your storm,
Fill their faces with shame,
Let them be ashamed and fearful forever;
Let them know that you alone,
For the leader. On the gittit. A psalm of the sons of Korach:
How deeply loved are your dwelling-places,
My soul yearns, yes, faints with longing
As the sparrow finds herself a home
How happy are those who live in your house;
How happy the man whose strength is in you,
Passing through the [dry] Baka Valley,
They go from strength to strength
Adonai, God of armies, hear my prayer;
God, see our shield [the king];
Better a day in your courtyards
For Adonai, God, is a sun and a shield;
Adonai-Tzva’ot,
For the leader. A psalm of the sons of Korach:
Adonai, you have shown favor to your land;
taken away the guilt of your people,
withdrawn all your wrath,
Restore us, God of our salvation,
Are you to stay angry with us forever?
Won’t you revive us again,
Show us your grace, Adonai;
I am listening. What will God, Adonai, say?
His salvation is near for those who fear him,
Grace and truth have met together;
Truth springs up from the earth,
Adonai will also grant prosperity;
Justice will walk before him
A prayer of David:
Preserve my life, for I am faithful;
Take pity on me, Adonai,
Fill your servant’s heart with joy,
Adonai, you are kind and forgiving,
Listen, Adonai, to my prayer;
On the day of my trouble I am calling on you,
There is none like you among the gods, Adonai;
All the nations you have made
For you are great, and you do wonders;
Adonai, teach me your way,
I will thank you, Adonai my God,
For your grace toward me is so great!
God, arrogant men are rising against me,
But you, Adonai,
Turn to me, and show me your favor;
Give me a sign of your favor,
A psalm of the sons of Korach. A song:
Adonai loves the gates of Tziyon
Glorious things are said about you,
I count Rahav and Bavel
But of Tziyon it will be said,
When he registers the peoples, Adonai will record,
Singers and dancers alike say,
A song. A psalm of the sons of Korach. For the leader. Set to “Sickness that Causes Suffering.” A maskil of Heiman the Ezrachi.
Adonai, God of my salvation,
let my prayer come before you,
For I am oversupplied with troubles,
I am counted among those going down to the pit,
left by myself among the dead,
You plunged me into the bottom of the pit,
Your wrath lies heavily on me;
You separated me from my close friends,
my eyes grow dim from suffering.
Will you perform wonders for the dead?
Will your grace be declared in the grave,
Will your wonders be known in the dark,
But I cry out to you, Adonai;
So why, Adonai, do you reject me?
Since my youth I have been miserable, close to death;
Your fierce anger has overwhelmed me,
They surge around me all day like a flood,
You have made friends and companions shun me;
A maskil of Eitan the Ezrachi:
I will sing about Adonai’s acts of grace forever,
because I said, “Grace is built to last forever;
You said, “I made a covenant with the one I chose,
‘I will establish your dynasty forever,
Let the heavens praise your wonders, Adonai,
For who in the skies can be compared with Adonai?
a God dreaded in the great assembly of the holy ones
Adonai Elohei-Tzva’ot!
You control the raging of the sea;
You crushed Rahav like a carcass;
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours;
You created north and south;
Your arm is mighty, your hand is strong,
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne;
How happy are the people who know the joyful shout!
They rejoice in your name all day
for you yourself are the strength in which they glory.
for our shield comes from Adonai —
There was a time when you spoke in a vision;
I have found David my servant
My hand will always be with him,
No enemy will outwit him,
I will crush his foes before him
My faithfulness and grace will be with him;
I will put his hand on the sea
He will call to me, ‘You are my father,
I will give him the position of firstborn,
I will keep my grace for him forever,
I will establish his dynasty forever,
“If his descendants abandon my Torah
if they profane my regulations
I will punish their disobedience with the rod
But I won’t withdraw my grace from him
I will not profane my covenant
I have sworn by my holiness once and for all;
his dynasty will last forever,
It will be established forever, like the moon,
But you spurned your anointed one,
You renounced the covenant with your servant
You broke through all his defenses
All who pass by plunder him;
You raised up the right hand of his foes
You drive back his drawn sword
You brought an end to his splendor
You cut short the days of his youth
How long, Adonai? Will you hide yourself forever?
Remember how little time I have!
Who can live and not see death?
Where, Adonai, are the acts of grace you once did,
Remember, Adonai, the taunts hurled at your servants,
Your enemies, Adonai, have flung their taunts,
Blessed be Adonai forever.
A prayer of Moshe the man of God:
Before the mountains were born,
You bring frail mortals to the point of being crushed,
For from your viewpoint a thousand years
When you sweep them away, they become like sleep;
growing and flowering in the morning,
For we are destroyed by your anger,
You have placed our faults before you,
All our days ebb away under your wrath;
The span of our life is seventy years,
Who grasps the power of your anger and wrath
So teach us to count our days,
Return, Adonai! How long must it go on?
Fill us at daybreak with your love,
Let our joy last as long as the time you made us suffer,
Show your deeds to your servants
May the favor of Adonai our God be on us,
You who live in the shelter of ‘Elyon,
who say to Adonai, “My refuge! My fortress!
he will rescue you from the trap of the hunter
he will cover you with his pinions,
You will not fear the terrors of night
or the plague that roams in the dark,
A thousand may fall at your side,
Only keep your eyes open,
For you have made Adonai, the Most High,
No disaster will happen to you,
for he will order his angels to care for you
They will carry you in their hands,
You will tread down lions and snakes,
“Because he loves me, I will rescue him;
He will call on me, and I will answer him.
I will satisfy him with long life
A psalm. A song for Shabbat:
It is good to give thanks to Adonai
to tell in the morning about your grace
to the music of a ten-stringed [harp] and a lute,
For, Adonai, what you do makes me happy;
How great are your deeds, Adonai!
Stupid people can’t know,
that when the wicked sprout like grass,
while you, Adonai, are exalted forever.
For your enemies, Adonai,
But you have given me
My eyes have gazed with pleasure on my enemies’ ruin,
The righteous will flourish like a palm tree,
Planted in the house of Adonai,
Even in old age they will be vigorous,
proclaiming that Adonai is upright,
Adonai is king, robed in majesty;
Your throne was established long ago;
Adonai, the deep is raising up,
More than the sound of rushing waters
Your instructions are very sure;
God of vengeance, Adonai!
Assert yourself as judge of the earth!
How long are the wicked, Adonai,
They pour out insolent words,
They crush your people, Adonai,
They kill widows and strangers
They say, “Yah isn’t looking;
Take notice, yourselves, you boors among the people!
Will the one who planted the ear not hear?
Will the one who disciplines nations not correct them?
Adonai understands that people’s thoughts
How happy the man whom you correct, Yah,
giving him respite from days of trouble,
For Adonai will not desert his people,
Justice will once again become righteous,
Who will champion my cause against the wicked?
If Adonai hadn’t helped me,
When I said, “My foot is slipping!”
When my cares within me are many,
Can unjust judges be allied with you,
They band together against the righteous
But Adonai has become my stronghold,
But he repays them as their guilt deserves;
Come, let’s sing to Adonai!
Let’s come into his presence with thanksgiving;

Let my lips speak praise,

how he swore to Adonai,
