Adonai does whatever pleases him,
He raises clouds from the ends of the earth,
He struck down Egypt’s firstborn,
He sent signs and wonders among you, Egypt,
He struck many nations,
Sichon king of the Emori,
Then he gave their land as a heritage,
Adonai, your name continues forever,
For Adonai will vindicate his people,
The idols of the nations are mere silver and gold,
They have mouths, but they can’t speak;
they have ears, but they can’t listen;
The people who make them will become like them,
House of Isra’el, bless Adonai!
House of Levi, bless Adonai!
Blessed be Adonai out of Tziyon,
Give thanks to Adonai, for he is good,
Give thanks to the God of gods,
Give thanks to the Lord of lords,
to him who alone has done great wonders,
to him who skillfully made the heavens,
to him who spread out the earth on the water,
to him who made the great lights,
the sun to rule the day,
the moon and stars to rule the night,
to him who struck down Egypt’s firstborn,
and brought Isra’el out from among them,
with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm,
to him who split apart the Sea of Suf,
and made Isra’el cross right through it,
but swept Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Suf,
to him who led his people through the desert,
to him who struck down great kings,
yes, he slaughtered powerful kings,
Sichon king of the Emori,
and ‘Og king of Bashan,
then he gave their land as a heritage,
to be possessed by Isra’el his servant,
who remembers us whenever we are brought low,
and rescues us from our enemies,
who provides food for every living creature,
Give thanks to the God of heaven,
By the rivers of Bavel we sat down and wept
We had hung up our lyres
when those who had taken us captive
How can we sing a song about Adonai
If I forget you, Yerushalayim,
May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth
Remember, Adonai, against the people of Edom
Daughter of Bavel, you will be destroyed!
A blessing on anyone who seizes your babies
By David:
I bow down toward your holy temple
When I called, you answered me,
All the kings of the earth will thank you, Adonai,
They will sing about Adonai’s ways,
For though Adonai is high, he cares for the lowly;
You keep me alive when surrounded by danger;
Adonai will fulfill his purpose for me.
For the leader. A psalm of David:
You know when I sit and when I stand up,
you scrutinize my daily activities.
that before I speak even a word, Adonai,
You have hemmed me in both behind and in front
Such wonderful knowledge is beyond me,
Where can I go to escape your Spirit?
If I climb up to heaven, you are there;
If I fly away with the wings of the dawn
even there your hand would lead me,
If I say, “Let darkness surround me,
even darkness like this
For you fashioned my inmost being,
I thank you because I am awesomely made,
My bones were not hidden from you
Your eyes could see me as an embryo,
God, how I prize your thoughts!
If I count them, there are more than grains of sand;
God, if only you would kill off the wicked!
They invoke your name for their crafty schemes;
Adonai, how I hate those who hate you!
I hate them with unlimited hatred!
Examine me, God, and know my heart;
See if there is in me any hurtful way,
For the leader. A psalm of David:
Rescue me, Adonai, from evil people,
They plan evil things in their hearts —
They have made their tongues as sharp as a snake’s;
Keep me, Adonai, from the hands of the wicked,
The arrogant hide snares for me;
I said to Adonai, “You are my God;
Adonai, Adonai, my saving strength,
Adonai, don’t grant the wicked their wishes;
May the heads of those who surround me
May burning coals rain down on them,
Let slanderers find no place in the land;
I know that Adonai gives justice to the poor
The righteous will surely give thanks to your name;
A psalm of David:
Let my prayer be like incense set before you,
Set a guard, Adonai, over my mouth;
Don’t let my heart turn to anything evil
Let the righteous strike me, let him correct me;
When their rulers are thrown down from the cliff,
As when one plows and breaks the ground into clods,
For my eyes, Adonai, Adonai, are on you;
Keep me from the trap they have set for me,
Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer:
With my voice I cry to Adonai,
Before him I pour out my complaint,
When my spirit faints within me,
Look to my right, and see
I cried out to you, Adonai;
Listen to my cry,
Lead me out of prison,
A psalm of David:
Don’t bring your servant to trial,
For an enemy is pursuing me;
My spirit faints within me;
I remember the days of old,
I spread out my hands to you,
Answer me quickly, Adonai,
Make me hear of your love in the morning,
Adonai, rescue me from my enemies;
Teach me to do your will,
For your name’s sake, Adonai, preserve my life;
In your grace, cut off my enemies;
By David:
He shows me grace; and he is my fortress,
Adonai, what are mere mortals,
Man is like a puff of wind,
Adonai, lower the heavens, and come down;
Shoot out lightning, and scatter them;
Reach out your hands from on high;
whose mouths speak worthless words
God, I will sing a new song to you;
You give kings their victories;
Rescue me, save me from the power of strangers,
Our sons in their youth will be
Our barns are full with crops of every kind;
our oxen are well-fed,
How happy the people who live in such conditions!
Praise. By David:
Every day I will bless you;
Great is Adonai and greatly to be praised;
Each generation will praise your works to the next
I will meditate on the glorious splendor
People will speak of your awesome power,
They will gush forth the fame of your abounding goodness,
Adonai is merciful and compassionate,
Adonai is good to all;
All your creatures will thank you, Adonai,
They will speak of the glory of your kingship,
to let everyone know of your mighty acts
Your kingship is an everlasting kingship,
Adonai supports all who fall
The eyes of all are looking to you;
You open your hand
Adonai is righteous in all his ways,
Adonai is close to all who call on him,
He fulfills the desire of those who fear him;
Adonai protects all who love him,
My mouth will proclaim the praise of Adonai;
Halleluyah!
I will praise Adonai as long as I live.
Don’t put your trust in princes
When they breathe their last, they return to dust;
Happy is he whose help is Ya‘akov’s God,
He made heaven and earth,
He secures justice for the oppressed,
Adonai opens the eyes of the blind,
Adonai watches over strangers,
Adonai will reign forever,
Halleluyah!
Adonai is rebuilding Yerushalayim,
He heals the brokenhearted
He determines how many stars there are
Our Lord is great, his power is vast,
Adonai sustains the humble
Sing to Adonai with thanks,
He veils the sky with clouds;
he gives food to the animals,
He takes no delight in the strength of a horse,
Adonai takes pleasure in those who fear him,
Glorify Adonai, Yerushalayim!
For he strengthens the bars of your gates,
he brings peace within your borders,
He sends his word out over the earth,
Thus he gives snow like wool,
sends crystals of ice like crumbs of bread —
Then he sends his word out and melts them;
He reveals his words to Ya‘akov,
He has not done this for other nations;
Halleluyah!
Praise him, all his angels!
Praise him, sun and moon!
Praise him, highest heaven,
Let them praise the name of Adonai;
He established them forever and ever;
Praise Adonai from the earth,
fire and hail, snow and mist,
mountains and every hill,
wild animals and all livestock,
kings of the earth and all peoples,
young men and women alike,
Let them praise the name of Adonai,
He has increased the power of his people,
Halleluyah!
Let Isra’el rejoice in their maker,
Let them praise his name with dancing,
for Adonai takes delight in his people,
Let the faithful exult gloriously,
Let the high praises of God be in their throats,
to carry out vengeance on the nations
to bind their kings with chains
to execute the judgments decreed for them;
Halleluyah!
Praise him for his mighty deeds!
Praise him with a blast on the shofar!
Praise him with tambourines and dancing!
Praise him with clanging cymbals!
Let everything that has breath praise Adonai!
The proverbs of Shlomo the son of David,
are for learning about wisdom and discipline;
for gaining an intelligently disciplined life,
for endowing with caution those who don’t think
Someone who is already wise
he will understand proverbs, obscure expressions,
The fear of Adonai is the beginning of knowledge,
My son, heed the discipline of your father,
they will be a garland to grace your head,
My son, if sinners entice you,
Suppose they say, “Come with us:
we’ll swallow him alive, like Sh’ol,
we’ll find everything he has of value,
Throw in your lot with us;
my son, don’t go along with them,
Their feet run to evil,
For in vain is the net baited
rather, they are ambushing themselves
So are the ways of all greedy for gain —
Wisdom calls aloud in the open air
she calls out at streetcorners
“How long, you whose lives have no purpose,
Repent when I reprove —
Because you refused when I called,
but instead you neglected my counsel
I, in turn, will laugh at your distress,
yes, when terror overtakes you like a storm
Then they will call me, but I won’t answer;
Because they hated knowledge
they refused my counsel
So they will bear the consequences of their own way
For the aimless wandering of the thoughtless will kill them,
but those who pay attention to me will live securely,
My son, if you will receive my words
paying attention to wisdom
yes, if you will call for insight
if you seek it as you would silver
then you will understand the fear of Adonai
For Adonai gives wisdom;
He stores up common sense for the upright,
in order to guard the courses of justice
Then you will understand righteousness, justice,
For wisdom will enter your heart,
discretion will watch over you,
They will save you from the way of evil
who leave the paths of honesty
who delight in doing evil
from those whose tracks are twisted
They will save you from a woman who is a stranger,
who abandons the ruler she had in her youth
Her house is sinking toward death,
None who go to her return;
Thus you will walk on the way of good people
For the upright will live in the land,
but the wicked will be cut off from the land,
My son, don’t forget my teaching,
for they will add to you many days,
Do not let grace and truth leave you —
Then you will win favor and esteem
Trust in Adonai with all your heart;
In all your ways acknowledge him;
Don’t be conceited about your own wisdom;
This will bring health to your body
Honor Adonai with your wealth
Then your granaries will be filled
My son, don’t despise Adonai’s discipline
for Adonai corrects those he loves
Happy the person who finds wisdom,
for her profit exceeds that of silver,
she is more precious than pearls —
Long life is in her right hand,
Her ways are pleasant ways,
She is a tree of life to those who grasp her;
Adonai by wisdom founded the earth,
by his knowledge the deep [springs] burst open
My son, don’t let these slip from your sight;
they will be life for your being
Then you will walk your way securely,
When you lie down, you will not be afraid;
Don’t be afraid of sudden terror or destruction
for you can rely on Adonai;
Don’t withhold good from someone entitled to it
Don’t tell your neighbor, “Go away! Come another time;
Don’t plan harm against your neighbor
Don’t quarrel with someone for no reason,
Don’t envy a man of violence,
for the perverse is an abomination to Adonai,
Adonai’s curse is in the house of the wicked,
The scornful he scorns,
The wise win honor,
Listen, children, to a father’s instruction;
for I am giving you good advice;
For I too was once a child to my father;
He too taught me; he said to me,
gain wisdom, gain insight;
Don’t abandon [wisdom]; then she will preserve you;
The beginning of wisdom is: get wisdom!
Cherish her, and she will exalt you;
she will give your head a garland of grace,
Listen, my son, receive what I say,
I’m directing you on the way of wisdom,
when you walk, your step won’t be hindered;
Hold fast to discipline, don’t let it go;
Don’t follow the path of the wicked
Avoid it, don’t go on it,
For they can’t sleep if they haven’t done evil,
For they eat the bread of wickedness
But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn,
The way of the wicked is like darkness;
My son, pay attention to what I am saying;
Don’t let them out of your sight,
for they are life to those who find them
Above everything else, guard your heart;
Keep crooked speech out of your mouth,
Let your eyes look straight ahead,
Level the path for your feet,
then deviate neither right nor left;
My son, pay attention to my wisdom;
so that you will preserve discretion
For the lips of a woman who is a stranger drop honey,
but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood,
Her feet go down to death,
she doesn’t walk the level path of life —
So now, children, listen to me;
distance your way from her,
so that you won’t give your vigor to others
so strangers won’t be filled with your strength
Then, when your flesh and bones have shrunk,
“How I hated discipline!
I ignored what my teachers said,
I took part in almost every kind of evil,
Drink the water from your own cistern,
Let what your springs produce be dispersed outside,
but let them be for you alone
Let your fountain, the wife of your youth,
a lovely deer, a graceful fawn;
My son, why be infatuated with an unknown woman?
For Adonai is watching a man’s ways;
A wicked person’s own crimes will trap him,
He will die from lack of discipline;
My son, if you have put up security for your friend,
you have been snared by the words of your mouth,
Do this now, my son, and extricate yourself,
give your eyes no sleep,
break free, like a gazelle from the [hunter’s] trap,
Go to the ant, you lazybones!
It has no chief, overseer or ruler;
yet it provides its food in summer
Lazybones! How long will you lie there in bed?
“I’ll just lie here a bit, rest a little longer,
and poverty comes marching in on you,
A scoundrel, a vicious man,
winking his eyes, shuffling his feet,
With deceit in his heart,
Therefore disaster suddenly overcomes him;
There are six things Adonai hates,
a haughty look, a lying tongue,
a heart that plots wicked schemes,
a false witness who lies with every breath,
My son, obey your father’s command,
Bind them always on your heart,
When you walk, they will lead you;
For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light,
They keep you from an evil woman,
Don’t let your heart lust after her beauty
The price of a whore is a loaf of bread,
Can a man carry fire inside his shirt
Can a man walk [barefoot] on hot coals
So is he who has sex with his neighbor’s wife;
A thief is not despised if he steals
but even he, if caught, must pay back sevenfold;
He who commits adultery lacks sense;
He will get nothing but blows and contempt,
For jealousy drives a man into a rage;
he will not accept compensation;
My son, keep my words,
Obey my commands, and live;
Bind them on your fingers;
Say to wisdom, “You are my sister”;
so that they can keep you from unknown women,
For I was at the window of my house,
when I saw among the young men there,
He crosses the street near her corner
Dusk turns into evening,
Then a woman approaches him,
She’s the coarse, impulsive type,
rather, she stalks the streets and squares,
She grabs him, gives him a kiss,
“I had to offer peace sacrifices,
This is why I came out to meet you,
I’ve spread quilts on my couch
I’ve perfumed my bed
Come on, let’s make love till morning;
My husband isn’t at home,
he took a bag of money with him
With all her sweet talk she convinces him,
At once he follows her
or like a bird rushing into a trap,
So now, children, listen to me;
Don’t let your heart turn to her ways;
For many are those she has struck down dead,
Her house is the way to Sh’ol;
Wisdom is calling!
On the heights along the road,
by the gates leading into the city,
“People, I am calling you,
You who don’t direct your lives,
“Listen! I will say worthwhile things;
My mouth says what is true,
All the words from my mouth are righteous;
They are all clear to those who understand
Receive my instruction, rather than silver;
For wisdom is better than pearls;
“I, wisdom, live together with caution;
The fear of Adonai is hatred of evil.
Good advice is mine, and common sense;
By me kings reign,
By me princes govern,
I love those who love me;
Riches and honor are with me,
My fruit is better than gold, fine gold,
I follow the course of righteousness
to endow with wealth those who love me
“Adonai made me as the beginning of his way,
I was appointed before the world,
When I was brought forth, there were no ocean depths,
I was brought forth before the hills,
he had not yet made the earth, the fields,
When he established the heavens, I was there.
when he set the skies above in place,
when he prescribed boundaries for the sea,
I was with him as someone he could trust.
playing everywhere on his earth,
“Therefore, children, listen to me:
Hear instruction, and grow wise;
How happy the person who listens to me,
For he who finds me finds life
But he who misses me harms himself;
Wisdom has built herself a house;
She has prepared her food, spiced her wine,
She has sent out her young girls [with invitations];
“Whoever is unsure of himself, turn in here!”
“Come and eat my food!
Don’t stay unsure of yourself, but live!
“He who corrects a scoffer only gets insulted;
If you reprove a scoffer, he will hate you;
Give to a wise man, and he grows still wiser;
The fear of Adonai is the beginning of wisdom,
For with me, your days will be increased;
If you are wise, your wisdom helps you;
The foolish woman is coarse;
She sits at the door of her house
calling to those who pass by,
“Whoever is unsure of himself, turn in here!”
“Stolen water is sweet;
But he doesn’t realize
The proverbs of Shlomo:
No good comes from ill-gotten wealth,
Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry,
Idle hands bring poverty;
A sensible person gathers in summer,
Blessings are for the head of the righteous,
The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing,
Wise-hearted people take orders,
He who walks purely walks securely,
He who winks his eye [instead of rebuking] causes pain,
The speech of the righteous is a fountain of life,
Hate stirs up disputes,
On the lips of the intelligent is found wisdom,
Wise people hide their knowledge,
The wealth of the rich is his fortified city;
The activity of the righteous is for life;
He who observes discipline is on the way to life;
He who covers up hate has lips that lie,
When words are many, sin is not lacking;
The tongue of the righteous is like pure silver,
The lips of the righteous feed many,
The blessing of Adonai is what makes people rich,
To a fool, vileness is like a game,
What a fool dreads will overtake him,
When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone;
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes
The fear of Adonai adds length to life,
What the righteous hope for will end in joy;
The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright
The righteous will never be moved,
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom,
The lips of the righteous know what is wanted,
False scales are an abomination to Adonai,
First comes pride, then disgrace;
The integrity of the upright guides them,
On the day of wrath, wealth doesn’t help;
The righteousness of the innocent levels their way,
The righteousness of the upright rescues them,
When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes;
The righteous is delivered from trouble,
With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor,
When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices;
By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up;
He who belittles another lacks good sense,
A gossip goes around revealing secrets,
Without clever tactics an army is defeated,
He who guarantees a loan for a stranger will suffer,
A gracious woman obtains honor;
A man who is kind does himself good,
The profits of the wicked are illusory;
Genuine righteousness leads to life,
The crooked-hearted are an abomination to Adonai,
Depend on it: the evil will not go unpunished;
Like a gold ring in the snout of a pig
The righteous desire only good,
Some give freely and still get richer,
The person who blesses others will prosper;
The people will curse him who withholds grain;
He who strives for good obtains favor,
He who trusts in his riches will fall,
Those who trouble their families inherit the wind,
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth,
He who loves knowledge loves discipline,
A good man obtains Adonai’s favor,
No one is made secure by wickedness,
A capable wife is a crown for her husband,
The plans of the righteous are just,
The words of the wicked are a deadly ambush,
Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them;
A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense,
Better to be despised and have a servant
A righteous man takes care of his animal,
He who farms his land will have plenty of food,
The wicked covet the loot of evil men,
The wicked is trapped by his own sinful speech,
One can be filled with good as the result of one’s words,
Fools suppose their way is straight,
A fool’s anger is known at once,
He who tells the truth furthers justice,
Idle talk can pierce like a sword,
Truthful words will stand forever,
Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil,
No harm can come to the righteous,
Lying lips are an abomination to Adonai,
A cautious person conceals knowledge,
The diligent will rule,
Anxiety in a person’s heart weighs him down,
The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly,
A lazy man doesn’t roast what he hunted;
In the road of righteousness is life;
A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise,
A [good] man enjoys good as a result of what he says,
He who guards his mouth preserves his life,
The lazy person wants but doesn’t have;
A righteous person hates lying,
Righteousness protects him whose way is honest,
There are those with nothing who pretend they are rich,
The rich man may have to ransom his life,
The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully,
Insolence produces only strife,
Wealth gotten by worthless means dwindles away,
Hope deferred makes the heart sick,
He who despises a word will suffer for it,
The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life,
Good common sense produces grace,
Every cautious person acts with knowledge,
A wicked messenger falls into evil,
Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught,
Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
He who walks with the wise will become wise,
Evil pursues sinners,
A good man leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren,
The fields of the poor may yield much food,
He who fails to use a stick hates his son,
The righteous person eats his fill,
Every wise woman builds up her home,
A person with upright conduct fears Adonai,
From the mouth of a fool sprouts pride,
Where there are no oxen, the stalls are clean;
An honest witness will not lie,
A scoffer seeks wisdom in vain,
Keep clear of a fool,
The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going,
Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools;
The heart knows its own bitterness,
The house of the wicked will be destroyed,
There can be a way which seems right to a person,
Even in laughter the heart can be sad,
A backslider is filled up with his own ways,
One who doesn’t think believes every word,
A wise person fears and turns away from evil,
He who is quick-tempered does stupid things,
Thoughtless people inherit folly,
The evil bow down before the good,
The poor are disliked even by their peers,
He who despises his fellow sins,
Won’t those who plot evil go astray?
In all work there is profit,
The crown of the wise is their riches,
A truthful witness saves lives,
In the fear of Adonai is powerful security;
The fear of Adonai is a fountain of life
A king’s glory lies in having many subjects;
Being slow to anger goes with great understanding,
A tranquil mind gives health to the body,
The oppressor of the poor insults his maker,
The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing,
Wisdom is at rest in a person with discernment,
Righteousness makes a nation great,
A king shows favor to a servant with good sense,
A gentle response deflects fury,
The tongue of the wise presents knowledge well,
The eyes of Adonai are everywhere,
A soothing tongue is a tree of life,
A fool despises his father’s discipline,
The home of the righteous is a storehouse of treasure,
The lips of the wise spread knowledge;
Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked
Adonai detests the way of the wicked
Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way,
Sh’ol and Abaddon lie open to Adonai;
A scorner does not like being corrected;
A glad heart makes a face happy,
The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge,
For the poor, every day is hard;
Better little with the fear of Adonai
Better a vegetable dinner with love
Hot-tempered people stir up strife,
The lazy person’s way seems overgrown by thorns,
A wise son is a joy to his father,
Folly appeals to one who lacks sense,
Without deliberation, plans go wrong;
People take pleasure in anything they say;
For the prudent, the path of life goes upward;
Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud,
Adonai detests plans to do evil,
The greedy for gain brings trouble to his home,
The mind of the righteous thinks before speaking,
Adonai is far from the wicked,
A cheerful glance brings joy to the heart,
He who heeds life-giving correction
He who spurns discipline detests himself,
The discipline of wisdom is fear of Adonai,
A person is responsible to prepare his heart,
All a man’s ways are pure in his own view,
If you entrust all you do to Adonai,
Adonai made everything for its purpose,
Adonai detests all those with proud hearts;
Grace and truth atone for iniquity,
When a man’s ways please Adonai,
Better a little with righteousness
A person may plan his path,
Divine inspiration is on the lips of the king,
The balance and scales of justice have their origin in Adonai;
It is an abomination for a king to do evil,
The king should delight in righteous lips,
The king’s anger is a herald of death,
When the king’s face brightens, it means life;
How much better than gold it is to gain wisdom!
Avoiding evil is the highway of the upright;
Pride goes before destruction,
Better to be humble among the poor
He who has skill in a matter will succeed;
A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment,
Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it,
The wise man’s heart teaches his mouth,
Pleasant words are like a honeycomb,
There can be a way which seems right to a person,
A working man’s appetite acts on his behalf,
A worthless person digs up evil [gossip] —
A deceitful person stirs up strife,
A violent man lures his neighbor astray
One who winks knowingly is planning deceit;
White hair is a crown of honor
He who controls his temper is better than a war hero,
One can cast lots into one’s lap,
Better a dry piece of bread with calm
An intelligent slave will rule a shameful son
The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold,
An evildoer heeds wicked lips;
He who mocks the poor insults his maker;
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged,
Fine speech is unbecoming to a boor,
A bribe works like a charm, in the view of him who gives it —
He who conceals an offense promotes love,
A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding
An evil person seeks only rebellion,
Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs
Evil will not depart from the house
Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] —
He who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous —
Why would a fool wish to pay for wisdom
A friend shows his friendship at all times —
He who gives his hand to guarantee a loan
Those who love quarreling love giving offense;
A crooked-hearted person will find nothing good,
He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow,
A happy heart is good medicine,
From under a cloak a bad man takes a bribe
The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him,
A son who is a fool means anger for his father
To punish the innocent is not right,
A knowledgeable person controls his tongue;
Even a fool, if he stays silent, is thought wise;
He who separates himself indulges his desires
A fool takes no pleasure in trying to understand;
When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too,
The words of a man’s mouth are deep water,
It is not good to be partial to the guilty
A fool’s words get him into fights;
A fool’s mouth is his ruin;
A slanderer’s words are tasty morsels;
Whoever is lazy in doing his work
The name of Adonai is a strong tower;
The wealth of the rich is his fortified city,
Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud;
To answer someone before hearing him out
A person’s spirit can sustain him when ill,
The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge,
A person’s gift clears his way
The first to state his case seems right,
Casting lots puts an end to strife
It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city;
A person’s belly will be filled with the fruit of his mouth;
The tongue has power over life and death;
He who finds a wife finds a great good;
The poor man speaks beseechingly,
Some “friends” pretend to be friends,
Better to be poor and live one’s life uprightly
To act without knowing how you function is not good;
A person’s own folly is what ruins his way,
Wealth brings in many friends,
A false witness will not go unpunished;
Many ask favors of a generous person —
A poor man’s relatives all hate him;
To acquire good sense is to love oneself;
A false witness will not go unpunished;
It isn’t fitting for a fool to live in luxury,
People with good sense are slow to anger,
A king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion,
A son who is a fool is his father’s ruin,
A house and wealth are inherited from ancestors,
Laziness makes people fall asleep,
He who keeps a mitzvah keeps himself safe,
He who is kind to the poor is lending to Adonai;
Discipline your child while there is hope,
A violent-tempered person will be punished;
Listen to advice, and accept discipline,
One can devise many plans in one’s mind,
A man’s lust is his shame,
The fear of Adonai leads to life;
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish
If you strike a scorner,
One who mistreats his father and evicts his mother
My son, if you stop heeding discipline,
A worthless witness mocks at justice,
Judgments are in store for scorners
Wine is a mocker, strong liquor a rowdy;
The dread of a king is like when a lion roars;
Avoiding quarrels brings a person honor;
A lazy person won’t plow in winter;
The heart’s real intentions are like deep water;
Most people announce that they show kindness,
The righteous live a life of integrity;
The king seated on his judgment throne
Who can say, “I have made my heart clean,
False weights and false measures —
The character of even a child is known by how he acts,
The hearing ear and the seeing eye —
If you love sleep, you will become poor;
“Really bad stuff!” says the buyer [to the seller];
A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls,
Seize his clothes, because he guaranteed a stranger’s loan;
Food obtained by fraud may taste good,
After consultation, plans succeed;
A gossip goes around revealing secrets,
Whoever curses his father or mother —
Possessions acquired quickly at first
Don’t say, “I’ll pay back evil for evil”;
Adonai detests a double standard in weights,
A man’s steps are ordered by Adonai,
It is a snare to dedicate a gift to God rashly
A wise king winnows the wicked [from the righteous]
The human spirit is a lamp of Adonai;
Grace and truth preserve a king;
The pride of the young is their strength;
Blows that wound purge away evil,
The king’s heart in Adonai’s hand is like streams of water —
All a person’s ways are right in his own view,
To do what is right and just
Haughty looks, a proud heart —
The plans of the diligent lead only to abundance;
A fortune gained by a lying tongue
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away,
A criminal’s conduct is crooked,
It is better to live on a corner of the roof
The wicked is set on evil;
When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser;
The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked;
Whoever stops up his ears at the cry of the poor
A secret gift allays anger,
Acting justly is a joy for the righteous
The person who strays from the way of common sense
Pleasure-lovers will suffer want;
The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous,
It is better to live in the desert
In the home of the wise are fine treasures and oil,
He who pursues righteousness and kindness
A wise man can go up into a city of warriors
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue
“Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person
A lazy man’s craving will kill him,
he covets greedily all day long;
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination;
A lying witness is doomed,
A wicked man puts on a bold face,
No wisdom, discernment or counsel
A horse may be prepared for the day of battle,
Rather than wealth, choose a good reputation,
Rich and poor have this in common —
The clever see trouble coming and hide;
The reward for humility is fear of Adonai,
Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn;
Train a child in the way he [should] go;
The rich rule the poor,
He who sows injustice reaps trouble,
He who is generous is blessed,
Throw the scoffer out, and quarreling goes too;
He who loves the pure-hearted and is gracious in speech
The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge,
A lazy man says, “There’s a lion outside!
The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit;
Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child,
Both oppressing the poor to enrich oneself
Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise;
for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you;
I want your trust to be in Adonai;
I have written you worthwhile things
so you will know that these sayings are certainly true
Don’t exploit the helpless, because they are helpless,
for Adonai will plead their case for them
Don’t associate with an angry man;
If you do, you may learn his ways
Don’t be one of those who give pledges,
for if you don’t have the wherewithal to pay,
Don’t move the ancient boundary stone
Do you see a man skilled at his work?
When you sit down to dine with a ruler,
If you have a big appetite,
Don’t be greedy for his delicacies,
Don’t exhaust yourself in pursuit of wealth;
If you make your eyes rush at it,
Don’t eat the food of a stingy man;
For he is like someone who keeps accounts —
The little you eat you will vomit up,
Don’t speak in the ears of a fool,
Don’t move the ancient boundary stone
for their Redeemer is strong;
Apply your mind to discipline
Don’t withhold discipline from a child —
If you beat him with a stick,
My son, if your heart is wise,
my inmost being rejoices
Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example
for then you will have a future;
You, my son: listen, be wise,
Don’t be one of those who guzzle wine
for both drunkard and glutton will become poor —
Listen to your father, who gave you life;
Buy the truth, don’t sell it,
A righteous person’s father will be filled with joy;
So let your father and mother be glad;
My son, give me your heart;
A prostitute is a deep ditch,
She lies in wait to snatch her prey
Who has misery? Who has regret?
Those who spend their time over wine,
Don’t gaze at the red wine
but in the end, it bites like a serpent —
Your eyes will see peculiar things,
You will feel as if lying on the waves of the sea
“They hit me, but I didn’t feel it!
Don’t be envious of evil people,
For their minds are occupied with violence,
By wisdom a house is built,
and by knowledge its rooms are filled
A wise man is strong;
For with clever strategy you wage your war,
Wisdom is too lofty for a fool;
He who plans to do evil
The evil plans of the foolish are sin,
If you slack off on a day of distress,
Yes, rescue those being dragged off to death —
If you say, “We knew nothing about it,”
My son, eat honey, for it is good;
Know that wisdom is similar[ly sweet] to your soul;
Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous,
For though he falls seven times, he will get up again;
Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls;
For Adonai might see it, and it would displease him;
Don’t get upset because of evildoers;
For the evil person has no future —
My son, don’t get involved with revolutionaries,
For disaster from them will suddenly appear,
These also are sayings of the wise:
He who tells the guilty, “You are innocent,”
but with those who condemn him, things will go well,
Giving an honest answer
Prepare your outside work,
Don’t be a witness against your neighbor for no reason —
Don’t say, “I’ll do to him what he did to me,
I passed by the field of the lazy man
There it was, overgrown with thistles;
I looked, and I thought about it;
“I’ll just lie here a bit, rest a little longer,
and poverty comes marching in on you,
These also are proverbs of Shlomo; the men of Hizkiyah king of Y’hudah copied them out:
God gets glory from concealing things;
Like the sky for height or the earth for depth
Remove the impurities from the silver,
Remove the wicked from the king’s presence,
Don’t put yourself forward in the king’s presence;
For it is better to be told, “Come up here,”
don’t rush to present in a dispute.
Discuss your dispute with your neighbor,
If you do, and he hears of it, he will disgrace you,
Like apples of gold in settings of silver
Like a gold earring, like a fine gold necklace
Like the coldness of snow in the heat of the harvest
Like clouds and wind that bring no rain
With patience a ruler may be won over,
If you find honey, eat only what you need;
so don’t visit your neighbor too much,
Like a club, a sword or a sharp arrow
Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble
Like removing clothes on a chilly day or like vinegar on soda
If someone who hates you is hungry, give him food to eat;
For you will heap fiery coals [of shame] on his head,
The north wind brings rain
It is better to live on a corner of the roof
Like cold water to a person faint from thirst
Like a muddied spring or a polluted well
It isn’t good to eat too much honey
Like a city breached, without walls,
Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time,
Like a fluttering sparrow or a flying swallow,
A whip for a horse, a bridle for a donkey,
Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly,
but answer a fool as his folly deserves,
Telling a message to a fool and sending him out
The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless;
Like one who ties his stone to the sling
Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk
A master can make anything,
Just as a dog returns to his vomit,
Do you see someone who thinks himself wise?
The lazy person says, “There’s a lion in the streets!
The door turns on its hinges,
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish
A lazy man is wiser in his own view
Like someone who grabs a dog by the ears
Like a madman shooting deadly arrows and firebrands
is one who deceives another, then says, “It was just a joke.”
If there’s no wood, the fire goes out;
As coals are to embers and wood to fire
A slanderer’s words are tasty morsels;
Like silver slag overlaid on a clay pot
He who hates may hide it with his speech;
He may speak pleasantly, but don’t trust him;
His hatred may be concealed by deceit,
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it,
A lying tongue hates its victims,
Don’t boast about tomorrow,
Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth,
Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight,
Fury is cruel and anger overwhelming,
Better open rebuke
Wounds from a friend are received as well-meant,
A person who is full loathes a honeycomb;
Like a bird that strays from its nest
Perfume and incense make the heart glad,
Don’t abandon a friend
My son, become wise, and gladden my heart,
The clever see trouble coming and hide;
Seize his clothes because he guaranteed a stranger’s loan;
Whoever greets his neighbor in a loud voice at dawn
A leak that keeps dripping on a rainy day
whoever can restrain her can restrain the wind
Just as iron sharpens iron,
Whoever tends the fig tree will eat its fruit,
Just as water reflects the face,
Sh’ol and Abaddon are never satisfied,
The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold,
You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle,
Take care to know the condition of your flocks,
For wealth doesn’t last forever,
When the hay has been mown, and the new grass appears,
the lambs will provide your clothing,
and there will be enough goat’s milk
The wicked flee when no one pursues them;
A land which transgresses [is punished by] having many rulers;
A poor man who oppresses the weak
Those who abandon Torah praise the wicked,
Evil people don’t understand justice,
Better to be poor and live an honest life
A wise son observes Torah,
He who increases his wealth by charging exorbitant interest
If a person will not listen to Torah,
Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways
The rich man is wise in his own view,
When the just are triumphant, there is great rejoicing,
He who conceals his sins will not succeed;
Happy the person who is never without fear,
Like a roaring lion or a bear prowling for food
A prince without discernment is a cruel oppressor,
Let a man weighed down with anyone’s blood
Whoever lives blamelessly will be saved,
He who farms his land will have plenty of food,
A trustworthy person will receive many blessings,
To show partiality is not good,
He who is greedy rushes after riches,
He who rebukes another person
Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!”
A grasping disposition stirs up strife,
He who trusts in himself is a fool,
He who gives to the poor will lack nothing,
When the wicked rise up, people hide;
He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke
When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice;
Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father,
A king gives stability to a country by justice,
A person who flatters his neighbor
In an evil person’s crime is a trap,
The righteous understands the cause of the poor,
Scoffers can inflame a city,
When a wise man argues with a foolish one,
Men of blood hate those who are pure
A fool gives vent to all his feelings,
If a ruler listens to lies,
The poor and the oppressor have this in common:
If a king steadfastly gives justice to the poor,
The rod and rebuke give wisdom,
When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes;
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest;
Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint;
A slave can’t be disciplined with words;
Do you see someone too anxious to speak?
A slave who is pampered from youth
Angry people stir up strife;
The proud will be humbled,
The accomplice of a thief hates himself;
Fearing human beings is a snare;
Many seek the ruler’s favor,
An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous,
The words of Agur the son of Yakeh, the prophecy. The man says to Iti’el, to Iti’el and Ukhal:
I am more boorish than anyone,
I have not learned enough wisdom
Who has gone up to heaven and come down?
Every word of God’s is pure;
Don’t add anything to his words;
[God,] I have asked two things of you;
keep falsehood and futility far from me,
for if I have too much, I might deny you
Never disparage a slave to his master,
There is a type of people who curse their fathers
There is a type of people clean in their own view,
There is a type of people — how haughty their look! —
There is a type of people whose teeth are like swords,
The leech has two daughters;
Sh’ol and a barren womb;
The eye that mocks his father
Three things are too wonderful for me,
the way of an eagle in the sky,
This is how an unfaithful wife behaves:
Three things make the earth quake,
a slave who becomes king,
a hated [wife] when her husband takes her [back],
Four things on the earth are small;
the ants, a species not strong,
the coneys, a species with little power,
the locusts, who have no king,
and the spiders, which you can catch in your hand,
Three things are stately in their stride,
the lion, mightiest of beasts,
the greyhound, the billy-goat
If you have been boorish, exalting yourself,
For as pressing milk produces butter
The words of King L’mu’el, the prophecy with which his mother disciplined him:
No, my son! No, son of my womb!
Don’t give your strength to women
It is not for kings, L’mu’el,
For they may drink, then forget what has been decreed,
Give strong liquor to one who is perishing,
let him drink, forget his poverty
Speak up for those who can’t speak for themselves,
Speak up, judge righteously,
Who can find a capable wife?
Her husband trusts her from his heart,
She works to bring him good, not harm,
She procures a supply of wool and flax
She is like those merchant vessels,
It’s still dark when she rises to give food to her household
She considers a field, then buys it,
She gathers her strength around her
She sees that her business affairs go well;
She puts her hands to the staff with the flax;
She reaches out to embrace the poor
When it snows, she has no fear for her household;
She makes her own quilts;
Her husband is known at the city gates
She makes linen garments and sells them;
Clothed with strength and dignity,
When she opens her mouth, she speaks wisely;
She watches how things go in her house,
Her children arise; they make her happy;
“Many women have done wonderful things,
Charm can lie, beauty can vanish,
Give her a share in what she produces;
The words of Kohelet the son of David, king in Yerushalayim:
Pointless! Pointless! — says Kohelet —
What does a person gain from all his labor
Generations come, generations go,
The sun rises, the sun sets;
The wind blows south,
All the rivers flow to the sea,
Everything is wearisome,
What has been is what will be,
Is there something of which it is said,
No one remembers the people of long ago;
I, Kohelet, have been king over Isra’el in Yerushalayim.
I wisely applied myself to seek out and investigate everything done under heaven. What a bothersome task God has given humanity to keep us occupied!
I have seen all the activities that are done under the sun, and it’s all pointless, feeding on wind.
What is crooked can’t be straightened;
I said to myself, “Look, I have acquired much wisdom, more than anyone ruling Yerushalayim before me.” Yes, I experienced a great deal of wisdom and knowledge;
yet when I applied myself to understanding wisdom and knowledge, as well as stupidity and folly, I came to see that this too was merely feeding on wind.
For in much wisdom is much grief;
I said to myself, “Come now, I will test myself with pleasure and enjoying good things”; but this too was pointless.
Of laughter I said, “This is stupid,” and of pleasure, “What’s the use of it?”

I searched my mind for how to gratify my body with wine and, with my mind still guiding me with wisdom, how to pursue foolishness; my object was to find out what was the best thing for people to do during the short time they have under heaven to live.
I worked on a grand scale — I built myself palaces, planted myself vineyards,
and made myself gardens and parks; in them I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
I made myself pools from which to water the trees springing up in the forest.
I bought male and female slaves, and I had my home-born slaves as well. I also had growing herds of cattle and flocks of sheep, more than anyone before me in Yerushalayim.
I amassed silver and gold, the wealth of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, things that provide sensual delight, and a good many concubines.
So I grew great, surpassing all who preceded me in Yerushalayim; my wisdom, too, stayed with me.
I denied my eyes nothing they wanted. I withheld no pleasure from myself; for I took pleasure in all my work, and this was my reward for all my work.
Then I looked at all that my hands had accomplished and at the work I had toiled at; and I saw that it was all meaningless and feeding on wind, and that there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
So I decided to look more carefully at wisdom, stupidity and foolishness; for what can the man who succeeds the king do, except what has already been done?
I saw that wisdom is more useful than foolishness, just as light is more useful than darkness.
The wise man has eyes in his head,
So I said to myself, “If the same thing happens to the fool as to me, then what did I gain by being wise?” and I thought to myself, “This too is pointless.
For the wise man, like the fool, will not be long remembered, inasmuch as in the times to come, everything will long ago have been forgotten. The wise man, no less than the fool, must die.”
So I came to hate life, because the activities done under the sun were loathesome to me, since everything is meaningless and feeding on wind.
I hated all the things for which I had worked under the sun, because I saw that I would have to leave them to the man who will come after me.
Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have control over all the things I worked for and which demonstrated how wise I am under the sun. This too is pointless.
Thus I came to despair over all the things I had worked for under the sun.
Here is a man whose work is done with wisdom, knowledge and skill; yet he has to leave it to someone who has put no work into it. This is not only pointless, but a great evil.
For what does a person get from all his efforts and ambitions permeating the work he does under the sun?
His whole life is one of pain, and his work is full of stress; even at night his mind gets no rest. This too is pointless.
So there is nothing better for a man to do than eat, drink and and let himself enjoy the good that results from his work. I also realized that this is from God’s hand.
For who will eat and who will enjoy except me?

For to the man who is good from [God’s] viewpoint he gives wisdom, knowledge and joy; but to the sinner he gives the task of collecting and accumulating things to leave to him who is good from God’s viewpoint. This too is pointless and feeding on wind.
For everything there is a season,
a time to be born and a time to die,
a time to kill and a time to heal,
a time to weep and a time to laugh,
a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones,
a time to search and a time to give up,
a time to tear and a time to sew,
a time to love and a time to hate,
What does the worker gain from his efforts?
I have seen the task God has given humanity to keep us occupied.
He has made everything suited to its time; also, he has given human beings an awareness of eternity; but in such a way that they can’t fully comprehend, from beginning to end, the things God does.
I know that there is nothing better for them to do than to be happy and enjoy themselves as long as they live.
Still, the fact that everyone can eat and drink and enjoy the good that results from all his work, is a gift of God.
I know that
That which was is here already;
Another thing I observed under the sun:
I said to myself, “The righteous and the wicked God will judge, because there is a right time for every intention and for every action.”
Concerning people, I said to myself, “God is testing them, so that they will see that by themselves they are just animals.

After all, the same things that happen to people happen to animals, the very same thing — just as the one dies, so does the other. Yes, their breath is the same; so that humans are no better than animals; since nothing matters, anyway.
They all go to the same place; they all come from dust, and they all return to dust.
Who knows if the spirit of a human being goes upward and the spirit of an animal goes downward into the earth?”
So I concluded that there is nothing better for a person to do than take joy in his activities, that that is his allotted portion; for who can enable him to see what will happen after him?
But I turned away and thought about all the kinds of oppression being done under the sun.
So I considered the dead happier, because they were already dead, than the living, who must still live their lives;
but happier than either of them is the one who has not yet been born, because he has not yet seen the evil things that are done under the sun.
Next I realized that all effort and achievement stem from one person’s envy of another. This too is futility and feeding on wind.
Fools fold their arms together
Better an armload with tranquillity
Then I turned my attention to something else under the sun that is pointless:

the situation in which a solitary individual without a companion, with neither son nor brother, keeps on working endlessly but never has enough wealth. “For whom” [he should ask], “am I working so hard and denying myself pleasure?” This too is truly pointless, a sorry business.
Two are better than one, in that their cooperative efforts yield this advantage:
if one of them falls, the other will help his partner up — woe to him who is alone when he falls and has no one to help him up.
Again, if two people sleep together, they keep each other warm; but how can one person be warm by himself?
Moreover, an attacker may defeat someone who is alone, but two can resist him; and a three-stranded cord is not easily broken.
Better a youth who is poor but wise
True, he rose from prison to be king;
I observed that all who live and walk under the sun took the side of the youth mentioned first who would rule in place of the king,
and that no limit was set for the number of his subjects. Nevertheless, those who come afterwards will not regard him highly. This too is certainly pointless and feeding on wind.
Watch your step when you go to the house of God. Offering to listen is better than fools offering sacrifices, because they don’t discern whether or not they are doing evil.
Don’t speak impulsively — don’t be in a hurry
For nightmares come from worrying too much;
If you make a vow to God, don’t delay in discharging it. For God takes no pleasure in fools, so discharge your vow!
Better not to make a vow than to make a vow and not discharge it.
Don’t let your words make you guilty, and don’t tell the temple official that you made the vow by mistake. Why give God reason to be angry at what you say and destroy what you have accomplished?
For [this is what happens when there are too] many dreams, aimless activities and words. Instead, just fear God!
If you see the poor oppressed, rights violated and justice perverted in the province, don’t be surprised; for a high official has one higher watching him, and there are others above them.
But the greatest advantage to the country is when the king makes himself a servant to the land.
The lover of money never has enough money;
When the quantity of goods increases,
The sleep of a working man is sweet,
Here is a gross evil which I have seen under the sun: the owner of wealth hoards it to his own hurt.
Due to some misfortune,
Just as he came from his mother’s womb,
This too is a gross evil, that in every respect as he came, so will he go; thus what profit does he have after toiling to earn the wind?
All his life he eats in darkness, in frustration, in sickness and in anger.

This is what I have seen to be good: that it is appropriate for a person to eat, drink and enjoy the good that results from all his work that he engages in under the sun for all the days of his life that God has given him, for this is his allotted portion.
Also, everyone to whom God has given riches and wealth, along with the power to enjoy it, so that he takes his allotted portion and finds pleasure in his work — this is a gift of God;
for he will not brood over the fact that his life is short, since God keeps him occupied with what will bring him joy.
I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on people:

the case in which God gives someone riches, wealth and honor, so that he lacks nothing that he wants; but God does not give him the power to enjoy them, and some stranger gets to enjoy them — this is meaningless, evil, sick.

Suppose a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that he has a long life, but he fails to enjoy himself; then, even if he were to [live indefinitely and therefore] never be buried, I say that it would be better to be born dead.
For the arrival of a stillborn baby is a futile thing, and its departure is in darkness; its name is [forgotten,] covered in darkness;
and although it has never seen or known the sun, it is more content than he is,
without enjoying himself, even if he were to live a thousand years twice over. Doesn’t everyone go to the same place?
The purpose of all toil is to fill the mouth,
What advantage has the wise over the fool,
Better what the eyes can see
Whatever he is, he was named long ago,
There are many things that only add to futility,
For who knows what is good for someone during life,
A good name is better than perfumed oil,
Better to go to a house of mourning
Grief is better than laughter,
The thoughts of the wise are in the house of mourning,
It is better to hear the rebukes of the wise
For the laughter of fools is like the crackling of thorns
But oppression can make a wise man stupid;
The end of something is better than its beginning,
Don’t be quick to get angry,
Don’t ask why the old days were better than now,
Wisdom is good, along with possessions,
For wisdom is a shelter,
Consider the work of God:
When things are going well, enjoy yourself;
In my pointless life, I’ve seen everything —
So don’t be overly righteous or overly wise;
But don’t be overly wicked, and don’t be foolish;

All this I have seen, as I applied my mind to everything done under the sun when one person tyrannizes another.
Thus I saw the wicked buried; they had even come from the Holy Place. But those who had acted uprightly were forgotten in the city. This too is a futile thing;
because the punishment decreed for an evil act is not promptly carried out; therefore people who plan to do evil are strengthened in their intentions.
For a sinner can do evil a hundred times and still live a long life; although I know that in the end things will go well with those who fear God, because they fear him.
But things will not go well with the wicked; and, like a shadow, he will not prolong his days; because he doesn’t fear God.

There is something frustrating that occurs on earth, namely, that there are righteous people to whom things happen as if they were doing wicked deeds; and, again, there are wicked people to whom things happen as if they were doing righteous deeds. I say that this too is pointless.

So I recommend enjoyment — a person can do nothing better under the sun than eat, drink and enjoy himself; this is what should accompany him as he does his work for as long as God gives him to live under the sun.
When I applied myself to gain wisdom and to observe how people occupy themselves on earth, that people’s eyes don’t see sleep either by day or by night,

then, on looking over all of God’s work, I realized that it is impossible to grasp all the activity taking place under the sun; because even if a person works hard at searching it out, he won’t grasp it; and even if a wise person thinks he knows it, he still won’t be able to grasp it.

I applied myself to all of this, sifted through it and concluded that the righteous and the wise, along with their deeds, are in God’s hands — a person cannot know whether these people and deeds will be rewarded with love or with hatred; all options are open.

Anything can happen to anyone; the same thing can happen to the righteous as to the wicked, to the good and clean and to the unclean, to someone who offers a sacrifice and to someone who doesn’t offer a sacrifice; it is the same for a good person as for a sinner, for someone who takes an oath rashly as for someone who fears to take an oath.

This is another evil among all those done under the sun, that the same events can occur to anyone. Truly, the human mind is full of evil; and as long as people live, folly is in their hearts; after which they go to be with the dead.
For as long as a person is linked with the living, there is hope — better to be a living dog than a dead lion!
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; there is no longer any reward for them, because all memory of them is lost.
What they loved, what they hated and what they envied all disappeared long ago, and they no longer have a share in anything done under the sun.
So go, eat your bread with joy,
Let your clothing always be white,

Enjoy life with the wife you have loved throughout your meaningless life that he has given you under the sun, all the days of your futility; for that is your allotted portion in life and in your labor that you work at under the sun.
Whatever task comes your way to do, do it with all your strength; because in Sh’ol, where you will go, there is neither working nor planning, neither knowledge nor wisdom.

Yet another thing I observed under the sun is that races aren’t won by the swift or battles by the strong, and that food doesn’t go to the wise or wealth to the intelligent or favor to the experts; rather, time and chance rule them all.

For people don’t know when their time will come any more than fish taken in the fatal net or birds caught in a snare; similarly, people are snared at an unfortunate time, when suddenly it falls on them.
Here is something else I have seen as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed important to me:
there was a small town with few people in it; and a great king came to attack it; he surrounded it and built massive siege-works against it.
Now there was found in it a man who was poor but wise, and by his wisdom he saved the city; yet afterwards, nobody remembered that poor man.
So, although I say that wisdom is better than strength, nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised; nobody pays attention to what he says.

Pointless! Meaningless! — says Kohelet,
Not only was Kohelet wise, he also taught the people what he knew; also he weighed, researched and corrected many ethical sayings.

The sayings of the wise are as sharp as goads, and those given by leaders of assemblies are like well-fixed nails; [in this case,] they are presented by a single shepherd.
In addition, my son, take heed: one can write many books — there’s no end to it; and one can study so much that it wearies the flesh.
Here is the final conclusion, now that you have heard everything: fear God, and keep his mitzvot; this is what being human is all about.
For God will bring to judgment everything we do, including every secret, whether good or bad.

It was in the fourteenth year of King Hizkiyahu that Sancheriv king of Ashur advanced against all the fortified cities of Y’hudah and captured them.

From Lakhish the king of Ashur sent Rav-Shakeh to Hizkiyahu in Yerushalayim with a large army. He positioned himself by the aqueduct from the Upper Pool, which is by the road to the Launderers’ Field.
Elyakim the son of Hilkiyahu, who was in charge of the household, Shevnah the general secretary and Yo’ach the son of Asaf the foreign minister went out to meet him.
Rav-Shakeh addressed them: “Tell Hizkiyahu: ‘Here is what the great king, the king of Ashur, says: “What makes you so confident?
I say: do mere words constitute strategy and strength for battle? In whom, then, are you trusting when you rebel against me like this?
Look! Relying on Egypt is like using a broken stick as a staff — when you lean on it, it punctures your hand. That’s what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like for anyone who puts his trust in him.
But if you tell me, ‘We trust in Adonai our God,’ then isn’t he the one whose high places and altars Hizkiyahu has removed, telling Y’hudah and Yerushalayim, ‘You must worship before this altar’?
All right, then, make a wager with my lord the king of Ashur: I will give you two thousand horses if you can find enough riders for them.
How then can you repulse even one of my master’s lowest-ranked army officers? Yet you are relying on Egypt for chariots and riders!
Do you think I have come up to this land to destroy it without Adonai’s approval? Adonai said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it!’ ” ’ ”
Elyakim, Shevnah and Yo’ach said to Rav-Shakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it; don’t speak to us in Hebrew while the people on the wall are listening.”

But Rav-Shakeh answered, “Did my master send me to deliver my message just to your master and yourselves? Didn’t he send me to address the men sitting on the wall, who, like you, are going to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
Then Rav-Shakeh stood up and, speaking loudly in Hebrew, said: “Hear what the great king, the king of Ashur, says!
This is what the king says: ‘Don’t let Hizkiyahu deceive you, because he won’t be able to save you.
And don’t let Hizkiyahu make you trust in Adonai by saying, “Adonai will surely save us; this city will not be given over to the king of Ashur.”
Don’t listen to Hizkiyahu.’ For this is what the king says: ‘Make peace with me, surrender to me. Then every one of you can eat from his vine and fig tree and drink the water in his own cistern,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land with grain and wine, a land with bread and vineyards.
Beware of Hizkiyahu; he is only deluding you when he says, “Adonai will save us.” Has any god of any nation ever saved his land from the power of the king of Ashur?
Where are the gods of Hamat and Arpad? Where are the gods of S’farvayim? Did they save Shomron from my power?
Where is the god of any of these countries that has saved its country from my power, so that Adonai might be able to save Yerushalayim from my power?’”
But they kept still and didn’t answer him so much as a word, for the king’s order was, “Don’t answer him.”

Then Elyakim the son of Hilkiyahu, who was in charge of the household, Shevnah the general secretary and Yo’ach the son of Asaf the foreign minister went to Hizkiyahu with their clothes torn and reported to him what Rav-Shakeh had said.
On hearing it, King Hizkiyahu tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth and entered the house of Adonai.
He sent Elyakim, who was in charge of the household, Shevnah the general secretary and the leading cohanim, covered with sackcloth, to Yesha‘yahu the prophet, the son of Amotz.
They said to him, “This is what Hizkiyahu says: ‘Today is a day of trouble, rebuke and disgrace. Children are ready to be born, but there is no strength to bring them to birth.

Maybe Adonai your God will hear the words of Rav-Shakeh, whom his master the king of Ashur has sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the message which Adonai your God has heard. So pray for the remnant that is left.’”
When King Hizkiyahu’s servants came to Yesha‘yahu,
he said to them, “Tell your master that this is what Adonai says: ‘Don’t be afraid of the words you heard the servants of the king of Ashur use to insult me.
I will put a spirit in him that will make him hear a rumor and return to his own land; then I will cause him to die by the sword in his own land.’”
Rav-Shakeh returned and, having heard that the king of Ashur had left Lakhish, found him making war with Livnah.
Then he heard it said that Tirhakah king of Ethiopia was on his way to fight him. On hearing this, the king of Ashur sent messengers to Hizkiyahu, after ordering them,
“This is what you are to say to Hizkiyahu king of Y’hudah: ‘Don’t let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, “Yerushalayim will not be handed over to the power of the king of Ashur.”
You have heard what the kings of Ashur have done to all lands — they have completely destroyed them. So how will you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them? No, my ancestors destroyed them — Gozan, Haran, Retzef and the people of ‘Eden who were in Tel’asar.
Where is the king of Hamat? the king of Arpad? the king of the city of S’farvayim, of Hena and ‘Ivah?’”
Hizkiyahu took the letter from the messengers’ hands and read it. Then Hizkiyahu went up to the house of Adonai and spread it out before Adonai.
This is the prayer that Hizkiyahu prayed to Adonai:
“Adonai-Tzva’ot, God of Isra’el, who dwells above the k’ruvim! You alone are God of all the kingdoms on earth. You made heaven and earth.
Turn your ear, Adonai, and hear! Open your eyes, Adonai, and see! Hear all the words that Sancheriv sent to taunt the living God.
It is true that the kings of Ashur have laid waste all the countries and their lands
and have thrown their gods into the fire. For those were non-gods, merely the products of people’s hands, wood and stone; this is why they could destroy them.
Now therefore, Adonai our God, save us from his power — so that all the kingdoms on earth will know that you are Adonai — you only.”
Then Yesha‘yahu the son of Amotz sent this message to Hizkiyahu: “Adonai the God of Isra’el says: ‘You prayed to me against Sancheriv king of Ashur.’

So Sancheriv king of Ashur left, went and returned to live in Ninveh.

One day, as he was worshipping in the temple of Nisrokh his god, his sons Adramelekh and Shar’etzer struck him with the sword and escaped into the land of Ararat. So his son Esar-Hadon took his place as king.

Around this time Hizkiyahu became ill to the point of death. Yesha‘yahu the prophet, the son of Amotz, came and said to him, “Here is what Adonai says: ‘Put your house in order, because you are going to die; you will not live.’”
Hizkiyahu turned his face toward the wall and prayed to Adonai:
“I plead with you, Adonai, remember now how I have lived before you truly and wholeheartedly, and how I have done what you see as good.” And he cried bitter tears.
Then the word of Adonai came to Yesha‘yahu:
“Go and tell Hizkiyahu that this is what Adonai, the God of David your ancestor, says: ‘I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; therefore I will add fifteen years to your life.
Also I will rescue you and this city from the power of the king of Ashur; I will defend this city.
The sign for you from Adonai that Adonai will do what he said is

that I will cause the shadow of the sundial, which has started going down on the sundial of Achaz, to go backward ten intervals.’” So the sun went back ten intervals of the distance it had already gone down.

Then Yesha‘yahu the prophet came to King Hizkiyahu and asked him, “What did these men say? Where did they come from?” Hizkiyahu answered, “They came to me from a distant country, Bavel.”

Now when the cohen Pash’chur son of Immer, chief official in the house of Adonai, heard Yirmeyahu prophesying these things,
he had him flogged and put him in the stocks at the Upper Binyamin Gate of the house of Adonai.
The following morning, when Pash’chur led Yirmeyahu out of the stocks, Yirmeyahu said to him, “Adonai no longer calls you Pash’chur but Magor-Missaviv [terror on every side].

For this is what Adonai says: ‘I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies, while you watch. I will hand over all of Y’hudah to the king of Bavel, and he will carry them off captive to Bavel and put them to the sword.

Moreover, I will hand over everything stored in this city, all its valuables, all its wealth, indeed all the treasures of the kings of Y’hudah, to their enemies, who will plunder them, take them and carry them to Bavel.
And you, Pash’chur, along with your entire household, will go into captivity; you will go to Bavel, where you will die and be buried — you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied lies.’”
You fooled me, Adonai; I have been your dupe.
Whenever I speak, I have to cry out;
But if I say, “I won’t think about him,
I have heard many whispering their plot:
But Adonai is with me like a dreaded warrior;
Adonai-Tzva’ot, you who test the righteous
Sing to Adonai! Praise Adonai!
A curse on the day I was born!
A curse on the man who brought the news
Let that man be like the cities
because God did not put me to death in the womb
Why did I have to emerge from the womb,
This is the word that came to Yirmeyahu from Adonai when King Tzidkiyahu sent to him Pash’chur the son of Malkiyah and Tz’fanyah the son of Ma‘aseiyah with this message:
“Please consult Adonai for us, because N’vukhadretzar king of Bavel is making war on us. Maybe Adonai will perform a miracle for us and cause him to withdraw.”
Yirmeyahu answered them, “Here is what you are to tell Tzidkiyahu:

‘This is what Adonai, the God of Isra’el, says: “I will make the weapons of war that you have in your hands ineffectual in your fight against the king of Bavel and the Kasdim who are outside the walls besieging you. Instead, I will gather them inside this city;
and I myself will fight against you with my hand stretched out and with a strong arm, in anger, rage and great fury.
I will strike the inhabitants of this city, humans and animals alike, and they will die of a terrible plague.

Afterwards,” says Adonai “I will hand over Tzidkiyahu king of Y’hudah, his servants, the people, and anyone remaining alive in this city after the plague, war and famine, to N’vukhadretzar king of Bavel and to their enemies, to those who seek their lives; and he will put them to the sword. He will not spare them; he will have no pity, no compassion.”’
“And here is what you are to tell this people: ‘Adonai says: “Look! I am presenting you with the way of life and the way of death.
Anyone who stays in this city will die by sword, famine and plague. But he who leaves and surrenders to the Kasdim besieging you will stay alive; his own life will be his only ‘spoils of war.’
For I have determined absolutely that this city will have evil, not good,” says Adonai. “It is going to be handed over to the king of Bavel, and he will burn it to the ground.”’
“To the royal house of Y’hudah say: ‘Hear the word of Adonai;
house of David, this is what Adonai says:
Adonai says, “I am against you, [Yerushalayim,]
I will punish you,” says Adonai,
Adonai said, “Go down to the house of the king of Y’hudah and there speak this word:
‘King of Y’hudah occupying David’s throne, hear the word of Adonai — you, your servants and your people who enter through these gates.
This is what Adonai says:
“‘“If you are careful to do this, then future kings occupying David’s throne will enter these palace gates riding in chariots and on horses — he, his servants and his people.
But if you will not pay attention to these words, then I swear by myself,” says Adonai, “that this palace will become a ruin.”’
“For here is what Adonai says concerning the palace of the king of Y’hudah:
I will designate men to destroy you,
“Many nations will pass by this city, and they will say to one another, ‘Why has Adonai done such a thing to this great city?’
The answer will be, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of Adonai their God and worshipped other gods, serving them.’”
Do not weep for [the king] who has died,
For this is what Adonai says about Shalum the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Y’hudah, who succeeded Yoshiyahu his father as king: “He has left this place, never to return;
but he will die in the place where they have led him captive, without seeing this land again.
“Woe to him who builds his palace unfairly,
who says, ‘I will build me a spacious palace
Your cedar may be excellent,
He upheld the cause of the poor and the weak,
“In contrast, your eyes and heart
Therefore here is what Adonai says concerning Y’hoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Y’hudah:
He will be given a donkey’s ‘burial’ —
Climb up to the L’vanon and cry out,
I spoke to you in your times of prosperity,
The wind will shepherd all your shepherds away,
You who live in the L’vanon,
“As I live,” says Adonai, “even if Koniyahu the son of Y’hoyakim king of Y’hudah were the signet ring on my right hand, I would pull you off
and hand you over to those who seek your life, to those you fear, N’vukhadretzar king of Bavel and the Kasdim.
I will hurl you and the mother who gave birth to you into a country different from the one you were born in, and you will die there.
They will not return to the country to which they long to return.”
Is this man Koniyahu
Oh, land, land, land!
This what Adonai says:
“Oh no! The shepherds are destroying and scattering the sheep in my pasture!” says Adonai.

Therefore this is what Adonai, the God of Isra’el, says against the shepherds who shepherd my people: “You have scattered my flock, driven them away and not taken care of them. So I will ‘take care of’ you because of your evil deeds,” says Adonai.
“I myself will gather what remains of my flock from all the countries where I have driven them and bring them back to their homes, and they will be fruitful and increase their numbers.
I will appoint shepherds over them who will shepherd them; then they will no longer be afraid or disgraced; and none will be missing,” says Adonai.
“The days are coming,” says Adonai
In his days Y’hudah will be saved,
“Therefore,” says Adonai, “the day will come when people no longer swear, ‘As Adonai lives, who brought the people of Isra’el out of the land of Egypt,’
but, ‘As Adonai lives, who brought the descendants of the house of Isra’el up from the land to the north’ and from all the countries where I drove them. Then they will live in their own land.”
Concerning the prophets:
For the land is full of adulterers;
“Both prophet and cohen are godless;
“Therefore their way will be slippery for them;
“I have seen inappropriate conduct
But in the prophets of Yerushalayim
Therefore, this is what Adonai-Tzva’ot says concerning the prophets:
Adonai-Tzva’ot says:
They keep reassuring those who despise me,
But which of them has been present at the council
Look! The storm of Adonai,
Adonai’s anger will not abate
“I did not send these prophets; yet they ran.
If they have been present at my council,
Am I God only when near,” asks Adonai,
Can anyone hide in a place so secret
“I have heard what these prophets prophesying lies in my name are saying: ‘I’ve had a dream! I’ve had a dream!’
How long will this go on? Is [my word] in the hearts of prophets who are prophesying lies, who are prophesying the deceit of their own minds?
With their dreams that they keep telling each other, they hope to cause my people to forget my name; just as their ancestors forgot my name when they worshipped Ba‘al.
“If a prophet has a dream,
“Isn’t my word like fire,” asks Adonai,
So, I am against the prophets,” says Adonai,
Yes, I am against the prophets,” says Adonai,

“I am against those who concoct prophecies out of fake dreams,” says Adonai. “They tell them, and by their lies and arrogance they lead my people astray. I didn’t send them, I didn’t commission them, and they don’t do this people any good at all,” says Adonai.
“When [someone from] this people, a prophet or a cohen asks you, ‘What is the burden of Adonai?’ you are to answer them, ‘What burden? I am throwing you off,’ says Adonai.
As for a prophet, cohen or [someone else from] this people who speaks about ‘the burden of Adonai,’ I will punish him and his household.”
So, when you speak with your neighbor or brother, ask, “What answer has Adonai given?” or “What has Adonai said?”
Don’t use the expression, “burden of Adonai” any more; for every person’s own word will be his burden. Must you twist the words of the living God, of Adonai-Tzva’ot, our God?
So, when speaking to a prophet, ask, “What answer has Adonai given you?” or “What did Adonai say?”

But if you talk about “the burden of Adonai,” then here is what Adonai says: “Because you use this expression, ‘the burden of Adonai,’ after I have already sent you the order not to say, ‘the burden of Adonai,’
I will lift you up, burden that you are, and throw you off, away from my presence — you and the city I gave you and your ancestors.
Then I will subject you to everlasting disgrace — eternal, unforgettable shame.”

It was after N’vukhadretzar king of Bavel had carried Y’khanyahu the son of Y’hoyakim, king of Y’hudah, along with the leaders of Y’hudah, the artisans and the skilled workers into exile from Yerushalayim and brought them to Bavel, that Adonai gave me a vision. There, in front of the temple of Adonai, two baskets of figs were placed.
